english.author: sujato
english.text: Long Discourses 33

english.author: sujato
english.text: Reciting in Concert

english.author: sujato
english.text: So I have heard.

segments.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā mallesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi yena pāvā nāma mallānaṁ nagaraṁ tadavasari.

english.author: sujato
english.text: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Mallas together with a large Saṅgha of five hundred mendicants when he arrived at a Mallian town named Pāvā.

segments.pali: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā pāvāyaṁ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There he stayed in Cunda the smith’s mango grove.

segments.pali: Tena kho pana samayena pāveyyakānaṁ mallānaṁ ubbhatakaṁ nāma navaṁ sandhāgāraṁ acirakāritaṁ hoti anajjhāvuṭṭhaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtena.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Now at that time a new town hall named Ubbhaṭaka had recently been constructed for the Mallas of Pāvā. It had not yet been occupied by an ascetic or brahmin or any human at all.

segments.pali: Assosuṁ kho pāveyyakā mallā: “bhagavā kira mallesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi pāvaṁ anuppatto pāvāyaṁ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane”ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The Mallas of Pāvā also heard that the Buddha had arrived and was staying in Cunda’s mango grove.

segments.pali: Atha kho pāveyyakā mallā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho pāveyyakā mallā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Then they went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segments.pali: “idha, bhante, pāveyyakānaṁ mallānaṁ ubbhatakaṁ nāma navaṁ sandhāgāraṁ acirakāritaṁ hoti anajjhāvuṭṭhaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtena.

english.author: sujato
english.text: “Sir, a new town hall named Ubbhaṭaka has recently been constructed for the Mallas of Pāvā. It has not yet been occupied by an ascetic or brahmin or any human at all.

segments.pali: Tañca kho, bhante, bhagavā paṭhamaṁ paribhuñjatu, bhagavatā paṭhamaṁ paribhuttaṁ pacchā pāveyyakā mallā paribhuñjissanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: May the Buddha be the first to use it, and only then will the Mallas of Pāvā use it.

segments.pali: Tadassa pāveyyakānaṁ mallānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That would be for the lasting welfare and happiness of the Mallas of Pāvā.”

english.author: sujato
english.text: The Buddha consented in silence.

segments.pali: Atha kho pāveyyakā mallā bhagavato adhivāsanaṁ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yena sandhāgāraṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā sabbasanthariṁ sandhāgāraṁ santharitvā bhagavato āsanāni paññāpetvā udakamaṇikaṁ patiṭṭhapetvā telapadīpaṁ āropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu;

english.author: sujato
english.text: Then, knowing that the Buddha had consented, the Mallas rose from their seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right. Then they went to the new town hall, where they spread carpets all over, prepared seats, set up a water jar, and placed an oil lamp. Then they went back to the Buddha,

english.author: sujato
english.text: bowed, stood to one side,

segments.pali: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho te pāveyyakā mallā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:

english.author: sujato
english.text: and told him of their preparations, saying,

segments.pali: “sabbasantharisanthataṁ, bhante, sandhāgāraṁ, bhagavato āsanāni paññattāni, udakamaṇiko patiṭṭhāpito, telapadīpo āropito.

english.author: sujato
english.text: “Please, sir, come at your convenience.”

segments.pali: Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṁ bhikkhusaṅghena yena sandhāgāraṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā pāde pakkhāletvā sandhāgāraṁ pavisitvā majjhimaṁ thambhaṁ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Then the Buddha robed up and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the new town hall together with the Saṅgha of mendicants. Having washed his feet he entered the town hall and sat against the central column facing east.

segments.pali: Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho pāde pakkhāletvā sandhāgāraṁ pavisitvā pacchimaṁ bhittiṁ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi bhagavantaṁyeva purakkhatvā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The Saṅgha of mendicants also washed their feet, entered the town hall, and sat against the west wall facing east, with the Buddha right in front of them.

segments.pali: Pāveyyakāpi kho mallā pāde pakkhāletvā sandhāgāraṁ pavisitvā puratthimaṁ bhittiṁ nissāya pacchimābhimukhā nisīdiṁsu bhagavantaṁyeva purakkhatvā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The Mallas of Pāvā also washed their feet, entered the town hall, and sat against the east wall facing west, with the Buddha right in front of them.

segments.pali: Atha kho bhagavā pāveyyake malle bahudeva rattiṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uyyojesi:

english.author: sujato
english.text: The Buddha spent much of the night educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the Mallas with a Dhamma talk. Then he sent them off,

english.author: sujato
english.text: “The night is getting late, Vāseṭṭhas.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Please go at your convenience.”

segments.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho pāveyyakā mallā bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkamiṁsu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: “Yes, sir,” replied the Mallas. They rose from their seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on their right, before leaving.

segments.pali: Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu pāveyyakesu mallesu tuṇhībhūtaṁ tuṇhībhūtaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ anuviloketvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Soon after they left, the Buddha looked around the Saṅgha of mendicants, who were so very silent. He addressed Venerable Sāriputta,

english.author: sujato
english.text: “Sāriputta, the Saṅgha of mendicants is rid of dullness and drowsiness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Give them some Dhamma talk as you feel inspired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: My back is sore,

english.author: sujato
english.text: I’ll stretch it.”

segments.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato paccassosi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: “Yes, sir,” Sāriputta replied.

segments.pali: Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṁ saṅghāṭiṁ paññāpetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappesi pāde pādaṁ accādhāya, sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṁ manasi karitvā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And then the Buddha spread out his outer robe folded in four and laid down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up.

segments.pali: Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto pāvāyaṁ adhunākālaṅkato hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Now at that time the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan had recently passed away at Pāvā.

segments.pali: Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṁ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti:

english.author: sujato
english.text: With his passing the Jain ascetics split, dividing into two factions, fighting, quarreling, and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words:

segments.pali: “na tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāsi, ahaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānāmi, kiṁ tvaṁ imaṁ dhammavinayaṁ ājānissasi. Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi, ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṁ me, asahitaṁ te. Purevacanīyaṁ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṁ pure avaca. Adhiciṇṇaṁ te viparāvattaṁ, āropito te vādo, niggahito tvamasi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī”ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: “You don’t understand this teaching and training. I understand this teaching and training. What, you understand this teaching and training? You’re practicing wrong. I’m practicing right. I stay on topic, you don’t. You said last what you should have said first. You said first what you should have said last. What you’ve thought so much about has been disproved. Your doctrine is refuted. Go on, save your doctrine! You’re trapped; get yourself out of this—if you can!”

segments.pali: Vadhoyeva kho maññe nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu vattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You’d think there was nothing but slaughter going on among the Jain ascetics.

segments.pali: Yepi nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā, tepi nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu nibbinnarūpā virattarūpā paṭivānarūpā, yathā taṁ durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṁvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And the Jain Ñātika’s white-clothed lay disciples were disillusioned, dismayed, and disappointed in the Jain ascetics. They were equally disappointed with a teaching and training so poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha, with broken monument and without a refuge.

segments.pali: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Then Sāriputta told the mendicants about these things. He went on to say,

segments.pali: tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā …pe… bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe.
Evañhetaṁ, āvuso, hoti durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṁvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite.

english.author: sujato
english.text: “That’s what happens, reverends, when a teaching and training is poorly explained and poorly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ kho panāvuso, amhākaṁ bhagavatā dhammo svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṁvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But this teaching is well explained and well propounded to us by the Blessed One, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ, na vivaditabbaṁ, yathayidaṁ brahmacariyaṁ addhaniyaṁ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṁ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite this in concert, without disputing, so that this spiritual path may last for a long time. That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segments.pali: Katamo cāvuso, amhākaṁ bhagavatā dhammo svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṁvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito;

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is that teaching?

segments.pali: yattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ, na vivaditabbaṁ, yathayidaṁ brahmacariyaṁ addhaniyaṁ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṁ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ?

english.author: sujato
english.text: 1. Ones

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena eko dhammo sammadakkhāto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by one that have been rightly explained by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ, na vivaditabbaṁ, yathayidaṁ brahmacariyaṁ addhaniyaṁ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṁ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert, without disputing, so that this spiritual path may last for a long time. That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by one?

english.author: sujato
english.text: All sentient beings are sustained by food.

english.author: sujato
english.text: All sentient beings are sustained by conditions.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena eko dhammo sammadakkhāto.

english.author: sujato

english.author: sujato

english.author: sujato

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ, na vivaditabbaṁ, yathayidaṁ brahmacariyaṁ addhaniyaṁ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṁ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

segments.pali: Saṁvego ca saṁvejanīyesu ṭhānesu saṁviggassa ca yoniso padhānaṁ.

english.author: sujato

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato

segments.pali: lobho akusalamūlaṁ, doso akusalamūlaṁ, moho akusalamūlaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of discrimination:

segments.pali: seyyohamasmīti vidhā, sadisohamasmīti vidhā, hīnohamasmīti vidhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’m better’, ‘I’m equal’, and ‘I’m worse’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three periods:

segments.pali: atīto addhā, anāgato addhā, paccuppanno addhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: past, future, and present.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three extremes:

segments.pali: sakkāyo anto, sakkāyasamudayo anto, sakkāyanirodho anto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: substantial reality, the origin of substantial reality, and the cessation of substantial reality.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three feelings:

segments.pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: pleasure, pain, and neutral.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three forms of suffering:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the suffering inherent in painful feeling, the suffering inherent in conditions, and the suffering inherent in perishing.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three heaps:

segments.pali: micchattaniyato rāsi, sammattaniyato rāsi, aniyato rāsi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the heap of surety in the wrong way, the heap of surety in the right way, and the heap of lack of surety.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three darknesses:

segments.pali: atītaṁ vā addhānaṁ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, anāgataṁ vā addhānaṁ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, etarahi vā paccuppannaṁ addhānaṁ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: one is doubtful, uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence about the past, future, and present.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three things a Realized One need not hide:

segments.pali: parisuddhakāyasamācāro āvuso tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa kāyaduccaritaṁ, yaṁ tathāgato rakkheyya:

english.author: sujato
english.text: The Realized One’s behavior by way of body, speech, and mind is pure. He has no misconduct in these three ways that need be hidden, thinking:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘Don’t let others find this out about me!’

segments.pali: Parisuddhavacīsamācāro āvuso, tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa vacīduccaritaṁ, yaṁ tathāgato rakkheyya:
Parisuddhamanosamācāro, āvuso, tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa manoduccaritaṁ yaṁ tathāgato rakkheyya:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three possessions:

segments.pali: rāgo kiñcanaṁ, doso kiñcanaṁ, moho kiñcanaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: greed, hate, and delusion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three fires:

english.author: sujato
english.text: greed, hate, and delusion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another three fires:

english.author: sujato
english.text: a fire for those worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, a fire for householders, and a fire for those worthy of a religious donation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Threefold classification of the physical:

segments.pali: sanidassanasappaṭighaṁ rūpaṁ, anidassanasappaṭighaṁ rūpaṁ, anidassanaappaṭighaṁ rūpaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: visible and resistant, invisible and resistant, and invisible and non-resistant.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three choices:

english.author: sujato
english.text: good choices, bad choices, and imperturbable choices.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three individuals:

segments.pali: sekkho puggalo, asekkho puggalo, nevasekkho nāsekkho puggalo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a trainee, an adept, and one who is neither a trainee nor an adept.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three seniors:

english.author: sujato
english.text: a senior by birth, a senior in the teaching, and a senior by convention.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three grounds for making merit:

segments.pali: dānamayaṁ puññakiriyavatthu, sīlamayaṁ puññakiriyavatthu, bhāvanāmayaṁ puññakiriyavatthu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: giving, ethical conduct, and meditation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three grounds for accusations:

english.author: sujato
english.text: what is seen, heard, and suspected.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of sensual rebirth:

segments.pali: santāvuso sattā paccupaṭṭhitakāmā, te paccupaṭṭhitesu kāmesu vasaṁ vattenti, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings who desire what is present. They fall under the sway of presently arisen sensual pleasures. Namely, humans, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first kind of sensual rebirth.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nimmitakāmā, te nimminitvā nimminitvā kāmesu vasaṁ vattenti, seyyathāpi devā nimmānaratī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings who desire to create. Having repeatedly created, they fall under the sway of sensual pleasures. Namely, the gods who love to create.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second kind of sensual rebirth.

segments.pali: Santāvuso sattā paranimmitakāmā, te paranimmitesu kāmesu vasaṁ vattenti, seyyathāpi devā paranimmitavasavattī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings who desire what is created by others. They fall under the sway of sensual pleasures created by others. Namely, the gods who control what is created by others.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third kind of sensual rebirth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of pleasant rebirth:

segments.pali: santāvuso sattā uppādetvā uppādetvā sukhaṁ viharanti, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings who, having repeatedly given rise to it, dwell in pleasure. Namely, the gods of the Divinity’s host.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first pleasant rebirth.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sukhena abhisannā parisannā paripūrā paripphuṭā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings who are drenched, steeped, filled, and soaked with pleasure.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Every so often they feel inspired to exclaim:

segments.pali: ‘aho sukhaṁ, aho sukhan’ti, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!’ Namely, the gods of streaming radiance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second pleasant rebirth.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sukhena abhisannā parisannā paripūrā paripphuṭā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings who are drenched, steeped, filled, and soaked with pleasure.

segments.pali: Te santaṁyeva tusitā sukhaṁ paṭisaṁvedenti, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Since they’re truly content, they experience pleasure. Namely, the gods of universal beauty.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third pleasant rebirth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of wisdom:

segments.pali: sekkhā paññā, asekkhā paññā, nevasekkhānāsekkhā paññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the wisdom of a trainee, the wisdom of an adept, and the wisdom of one who is neither a trainee nor an adept.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another three kinds of wisdom:

segments.pali: cintāmayā paññā, sutamayā paññā, bhāvanāmayā paññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: wisdom produced by thought, learning, and meditation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three weapons:

english.author: sujato
english.text: learning, seclusion, and wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three faculties:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the faculty of understanding that enlightenment is imminent, the faculty of enlightenment, and the faculty of one who is enlightened.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three eyes:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the eye of the flesh, the eye of clairvoyance, and the eye of wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three trainings:

english.author: sujato
english.text: in higher ethics, higher mind, and higher wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of development:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the development of physical endurance, the development of the mind, and the development of wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three unsurpassable qualities:

english.author: sujato
english.text: unsurpassable seeing, practice, and freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of immersion:

segments.pali: savitakkasavicāro samādhi, avitakkavicāramatto samādhi, avitakkaavicāro samādhi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Immersion with placing the mind and keeping it connected. Immersion without placing the mind, merely keeping it connected. Immersion without placing the mind or keeping it connected.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another three kinds of immersion:

segments.pali: suññato samādhi, animitto samādhi, appaṇihito samādhi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: emptiness, signless, and undirected.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three purities:

english.author: sujato
english.text: purity of body, speech, and mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three kinds of sagacity:

english.author: sujato
english.text: sagacity of body, speech, and mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three skills:

english.author: sujato
english.text: skill in progress, skill in regress, and skill in means.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three vanities:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the vanity of health, the vanity of youth, and the vanity of life.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three ways of putting something in charge:

english.author: sujato
english.text: putting oneself, the world, or the teaching in charge.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three topics of discussion:

segments.pali: atītaṁ vā addhānaṁ ārabbha kathaṁ katheyya:

english.author: sujato
english.text: You might discuss the past:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘That is how it was in the past.’

segments.pali: anāgataṁ vā addhānaṁ ārabbha kathaṁ katheyya:

english.author: sujato
english.text: You might discuss the future:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘That is how it will be in the future.’

segments.pali: etarahi vā paccuppannaṁ addhānaṁ ārabbha kathaṁ katheyya:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or you might discuss the present:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘This is how it is at present.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three knowledges:

segments.pali: pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṁ vijjā, sattānaṁ cutūpapāteñāṇaṁ vijjā, āsavānaṁ khayeñāṇaṁ vijjā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: recollection of past lives, knowledge of the death and rebirth of sentient beings, and knowledge of the ending of defilements.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three meditative abidings:

segments.pali: dibbo vihāro, brahmā vihāro, ariyo vihāro.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the heavenly meditation, the divine meditation, and the noble meditation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Three demonstrations:

english.author: sujato
english.text: The demonstration of psychic power, the demonstration of revealing, and the demonstration of instruction.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by three that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 4. Fours

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by four that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ, na vivaditabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by four?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four kinds of mindfulness meditation:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

english.author: sujato
english.text: mind …

segments.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four right efforts:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu anuppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ anuppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

segments.pali: Uppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up.

segments.pali: Anuppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ uppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.

segments.pali: Uppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are completed by development.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four bases of psychic power:

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to mental development, and active effort.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy, and active effort.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to inquiry, and active effort.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four absorptions:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segments.pali: Vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segments.pali: Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, personally experiencing the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

segments.pali: Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā, adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ways of developing immersion further:

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to blissful meditation in this life.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ñāṇadassanapaṭilābhāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satisampajaññāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to mindfulness and awareness.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to the ending of defilements.

segments.pali: Katamā cāvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to blissful meditation in this life?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption …

english.author: sujato
english.text: second absorption …

english.author: sujato
english.text: fourth absorption.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ, āvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to blissful meditation in this life.

segments.pali: Katamā cāvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ñāṇadassanapaṭilābhāya saṁvattati?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ālokasaññaṁ manasi karoti, divāsaññaṁ adhiṭṭhāti yathā divā tathā rattiṁ, yathā rattiṁ tathā divā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant applies their mind to the perception of light, focusing on the perception of day regardless of whether it’s night or day.

segments.pali: Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ, āvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ñāṇadassanapaṭilābhāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision.

segments.pali: Katamā cāvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satisampajaññāya saṁvattati?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to mindfulness and awareness?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno viditā vedanā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant knows feelings as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

segments.pali: Viditā saññā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They know perceptions as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

segments.pali: Viditā vitakkā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They know thoughts as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ, āvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satisampajaññāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to mindfulness and awareness.

segments.pali: Katamā cāvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattati?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to the ending of defilements?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassī viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

segments.pali: Iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Such are feelings …

english.author: sujato
english.text: perceptions …

english.author: sujato
english.text: choices …

segments.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness.’

segments.pali: Ayaṁ, āvuso, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to the ending of defilements.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four limitless states:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṁ. Tathā tatiyaṁ. Tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They meditate spreading a heart full of compassion …

english.author: sujato
english.text: rejoicing …

segments.pali: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṁ. Tathā tatiyaṁ. Tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four formless states:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four supports:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṁ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṁ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṁ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṁ vinodeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: After appraisal, a mendicant uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and gets rid of some things.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four noble traditions:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena cīvarena, itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, na ca cīvarahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca cīvaraṁ na paritassati, laddhā ca cīvaraṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati; tāya ca pana itarītaracīvarasantuṭṭhiyā nevattānukkaṁseti na paraṁ vambheti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant is content with any kind of robe, and praises such contentment. They don’t employ improper solicitation for the sake of a robe. They don’t worry if they don’t get a robe. And if they do get a robe, they use it untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawback, and understanding the escape. And on account of that they don’t glorify themselves or put others down.

segments.pali: Yo hi tattha dakkho analaso sampajāno paṭissato, ayaṁ vuccatāvuso: ‘bhikkhu porāṇe aggaññe ariyavaṁse ṭhito’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant who is deft, tireless, aware, and mindful in this is said to stand in the ancient, primordial noble tradition.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena piṇḍapātena, itarītarapiṇḍapātasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, na ca piṇḍapātahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca piṇḍapātaṁ na paritassati, laddhā ca piṇḍapātaṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati; tāya ca pana itarītarapiṇḍapātasantuṭṭhiyā nevattānukkaṁseti na paraṁ vambheti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is content with any kind of almsfood …

segments.pali: Yo hi tattha dakkho analaso sampajāno paṭissato, ayaṁ vuccatāvuso: ‘bhikkhu porāṇe aggaññe ariyavaṁse ṭhito’.

Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarena senāsanena, itarītarasenāsanasantuṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇavādī, na ca senāsanahetu anesanaṁ appatirūpaṁ āpajjati; aladdhā ca senāsanaṁ na paritassati, laddhā ca senāsanaṁ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati; tāya ca pana itarītarasenāsanasantuṭṭhiyā nevattānukkaṁseti na paraṁ vambheti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is content with any kind of lodgings …

segments.pali: Yo hi tattha dakkho analaso sampajāno paṭissato, ayaṁ vuccatāvuso: ‘bhikkhu porāṇe aggaññe ariyavaṁse ṭhito’.
Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu pahānārāmo hoti pahānarato, bhāvanārāmo hoti bhāvanārato; tāya ca pana pahānārāmatāya pahānaratiyā bhāvanārāmatāya bhāvanāratiyā nevattānukkaṁseti na paraṁ vambheti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant enjoys giving up and loves to give up. They enjoy meditation and love to meditate. But they don’t glorify themselves or put down others on account of their love for giving up and meditation.

segments.pali: Yo hi tattha dakkho analaso sampajāno paṭissato ayaṁ vuccatāvuso: ‘bhikkhu porāṇe aggaññe ariyavaṁse ṭhito’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant who is deft, tireless, aware, and mindful in this is said to stand in the ancient, primordial noble tradition.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four efforts:

english.author: sujato
english.text: The efforts to restrain, to give up, to develop, and to preserve.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the effort to restrain?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segments.pali: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ, cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.

english.author: sujato
english.text: When they hear a sound with their ears …

english.author: sujato
english.text: When they smell an odor with their nose …

english.author: sujato
english.text: When they taste a flavor with their tongue …

english.author: sujato
english.text: When they feel a touch with their body …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segments.pali: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṁ, manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is called the effort to restrain.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the effort to give up?

segments.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantiṁ karoti anabhāvaṁ gameti;

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual,

english.author: sujato
english.text: malicious,

english.author: sujato
english.text: or cruel thought that’s arisen, but gives it up, gets rid of it, eliminates it, and obliterates it.

segments.pali: uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantiṁ karoti anabhāvaṁ gameti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, get rid of them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is called the effort to give up.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the effort to develop?

segments.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ,

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant develops the awakening factors of mindfulness,

english.author: sujato
english.text: investigation of principles,

english.author: sujato
english.text: energy,

english.author: sujato
english.text: rapture,

english.author: sujato
english.text: tranquility,

english.author: sujato
english.text: immersion,

segments.pali: upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is called the effort to develop.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And what is the effort to preserve?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu uppannaṁ bhadrakaṁ samādhinimittaṁ anurakkhati—aṭṭhikasaññaṁ, puḷuvakasaññaṁ, vinīlakasaññaṁ, vicchiddakasaññaṁ, uddhumātakasaññaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant preserves a meditation subject that’s a fine basis of immersion: the perception of a skeleton, a worm-infested corpse, a livid corpse, a split open corpse, or a bloated corpse.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is called the effort to preserve.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four knowledges:

segments.pali: dhamme ñāṇaṁ, anvaye ñāṇaṁ, pariye ñāṇaṁ, sammutiyā ñāṇaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: knowledge of the teaching, inferential knowledge, knowledge of encompassing, and conventional knowledge.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four knowledges:

segments.pali: dukkhe ñāṇaṁ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṁ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṁ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: knowing about suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four factors for stream-entry:

english.author: sujato
english.text: associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four factors of a stream-enterer:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:

english.author: sujato
english.text: A noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segments.pali: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho, bhagavā’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segments.pali: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segments.pali: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segments.pali: Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four fruits of the ascetic life:

english.author: sujato
english.text: stream-entry, once-return, non-return, and perfection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four elements:

english.author: sujato
english.text: earth, water, fire, and air.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four foods:

segments.pali: kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṁ catutthaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: edible food, whether solid or subtle; contact is the second, mental intention the third, and consciousness the fourth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four grounds for consciousness:

segments.pali: Rūpūpāyaṁ vā, āvuso, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭhati rūpārammaṇaṁ rūpappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjati;

english.author: sujato
english.text: As long as consciousness continues, it gets involved with form, supported by form, established on form. And with a sprinkle of relishing, it grows, increases, and matures.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or consciousness gets involved with feeling …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or consciousness gets involved with perception …

segments.pali: saṅkhārūpāyaṁ vā, āvuso, viññāṇaṁ tiṭṭhamānaṁ tiṭṭhati saṅkhārārammaṇaṁ saṅkhārappatiṭṭhaṁ nandūpasecanaṁ vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or as long as consciousness continues, it gets involved with choices, supported by choices, established on choices. And with a sprinkle of relishing, it grows, increases, and matures.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four prejudices:

segments.pali: chandāgatiṁ gacchati, dosāgatiṁ gacchati, mohāgatiṁ gacchati, bhayāgatiṁ gacchati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: making decisions prejudiced by favoritism, hostility, stupidity, and cowardice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four things that give rise to craving:

segments.pali: cīvarahetu vā, āvuso, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati;

english.author: sujato
english.text: Craving arises in a mendicant for the sake of robes,

segments.pali: piṇḍapātahetu vā, āvuso, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati;

english.author: sujato
english.text: almsfood,

segments.pali: senāsanahetu vā, āvuso, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati;

english.author: sujato
english.text: lodgings,

segments.pali: itibhavābhavahetu vā, āvuso, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: or rebirth in this or that state.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ways of practice:

segments.pali: dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā, dukkhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā, sukhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā, sukhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: painful practice with slow insight, painful practice with swift insight, pleasant practice with slow insight, and pleasant practice with swift insight.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four ways of practice:

segments.pali: akkhamā paṭipadā, khamā paṭipadā, damā paṭipadā, samā paṭipadā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: impatient practice, patient practice, taming practice, and calming practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four footprints of the Dhamma:

segments.pali: anabhijjhā dhammapadaṁ, abyāpādo dhammapadaṁ, sammāsati dhammapadaṁ, sammāsamādhi dhammapadaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: contentment, good will, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ways of taking up practices:

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of taking up practices that is painful now and results in future pain.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of taking up practices that is painful now but results in future pleasure.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of taking up practices that is pleasant now but results in future pain.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a way of taking up practices that is pleasant now and results in future pleasure.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four spectrums of the teaching:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ethics, immersion, wisdom, and freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four powers:

english.author: sujato
english.text: energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four foundations:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the foundations of wisdom, truth, generosity, and peace.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ways of answering questions:

segments.pali: ekaṁsabyākaraṇīyo pañho, paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho, vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho, ṭhapanīyo pañho.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is a question that should be answered categorically. There is a question that should be answered analytically. There is a question that should be answered with a counter-question. There is a question that should be set aside.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four deeds:

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are deeds that are dark with dark result.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are deeds that are bright with bright result.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are deeds that are dark and bright with dark and bright result.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, kammaṁ akaṇhaasukkaṁ akaṇhaasukkavipākaṁ kammakkhayāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are neither dark nor bright deeds with neither dark nor bright results, which lead to the ending of deeds.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four things to be realized:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Past lives are to be realized with recollection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The passing away and rebirth of sentient beings is to be realized with vision.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The eight liberations are to be realized with direct meditative experience.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The ending of defilements is to be realized with wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four floods:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the floods of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four yokes:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the yokes of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four unyokings:

english.author: sujato
english.text: unyoking from the yokes of sensuality, desire for rebirth, views, and ignorance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ties:

segments.pali: abhijjhā kāyagantho, byāpādo kāyagantho, sīlabbataparāmāso kāyagantho, idaṁsaccābhiniveso kāyagantho.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the personal ties to covetousness, ill will, misapprehension of precepts and observances, and the insistence that this is the only truth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four kinds of grasping:

english.author: sujato
english.text: grasping at sensual pleasures, views, precepts and observances, and theories of a self.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four kinds of reproduction:

english.author: sujato
english.text: reproduction for creatures born from an egg, from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four kinds of conception:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco asampajāno mātukucchiṁ okkamati, asampajāno mātukucchismiṁ ṭhāti, asampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṁ paṭhamā gabbhāvakkanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone is unaware when conceived in their mother’s womb, unaware as they remain there, and unaware as they emerge. This is the first kind of conception.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, idhekacco sampajāno mātukucchiṁ okkamati, asampajāno mātukucchismiṁ ṭhāti, asampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṁ dutiyā gabbhāvakkanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, someone is aware when conceived in their mother’s womb, but unaware as they remain there, and unaware as they emerge. This is the second kind of conception.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, idhekacco sampajāno mātukucchiṁ okkamati, sampajāno mātukucchismiṁ ṭhāti, asampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṁ tatiyā gabbhāvakkanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, someone is aware when conceived in their mother’s womb, aware as they remain there, but unaware as they emerge. This is the third kind of conception.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, idhekacco sampajāno mātukucchiṁ okkamati, sampajāno mātukucchismiṁ ṭhāti, sampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, ayaṁ catutthā gabbhāvakkanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, someone is aware when conceived in their mother’s womb, aware as they remain there, and aware as they emerge. This is the fourth kind of conception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four kinds of incarnation:

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe attasañcetanāyeva kamati, no parasañcetanā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is an incarnation where only one’s own intention is effective, not that of others.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe parasañcetanāyeva kamati, no attasañcetanā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is an incarnation where only the intention of others is effective, not one’s own.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe attasañcetanā ceva kamati parasañcetanā ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is an incarnation where both one’s own and others’ intentions are effective.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe neva attasañcetanā kamati, no parasañcetanā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There is an incarnation where neither one’s own nor others’ intentions are effective.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ways of purifying a religious donation:

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the giver, not the recipient.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati no dāyakato.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the recipient, not the giver.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati no paṭiggāhakato.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by neither the giver nor the recipient.

segments.pali: Atthāvuso, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by both the giver and the recipient.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ways of being inclusive:

english.author: sujato
english.text: giving, kindly words, taking care, and equality.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four ignoble expressions:

english.author: sujato
english.text: speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four noble expressions:

segments.pali: musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: refraining from speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four ignoble expressions:

segments.pali: adiṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, assute sutavāditā, amute mutavāditā, aviññāte viññātavāditā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: saying you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known something, but you haven’t.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four noble expressions:

segments.pali: adiṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, assute assutavāditā, amute amutavāditā, aviññāte aviññātavāditā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: saying you haven’t seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you haven’t.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four ignoble expressions:

segments.pali: diṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, sute assutavāditā, mute amutavāditā, viññāte aviññātavāditā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: saying you haven’t seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you have.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four noble expressions:

segments.pali: diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, sute sutavāditā, mute mutavāditā, viññāte viññātavāditā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: saying you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you have.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Four individuals:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo attantapo hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual mortifies themselves, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo parantapo hoti paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual mortifies others, committed to the practice of mortifying others.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo attantapo ca hoti attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto, parantapo ca paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual mortifies themselves and others, committed to the practice of mortifying themselves and others.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo neva attantapo hoti na attaparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto na parantapo na paraparitāpanānuyogamanuyutto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual doesn’t mortify either themselves or others, committed to the practice of not mortifying themselves or others.

segments.pali: So anattantapo aparantapo diṭṭheva dhamme nicchāto nibbuto sītībhūto sukhappaṭisaṁvedī brahmabhūtena attanā viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They live without wishes in this very life, quenched, cooled, experiencing bliss, with self become divine.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four individuals:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti no parahitāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti no attahitāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo neva attahitāya paṭipanno hoti no parahitāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: One individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four individuals:

segments.pali: tamo tamaparāyano, tamo jotiparāyano, joti tamaparāyano, joti jotiparāyano.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the dark bound for darkness, the dark bound for light, the light bound for darkness, and the light bound for light.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another four individuals:

english.author: sujato
english.text: the confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by four that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The first recitation section is complete.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 5. Fives

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena pañca dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by five that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by five?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five aggregates:

english.author: sujato
english.text: form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five grasping aggregates:

english.author: sujato
english.text: form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five kinds of sensual stimulation:

segments.pali: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasañhitā rajanīyā,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Sounds known by the ear …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Smells known by the nose …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Tastes known by the tongue …

segments.pali: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasañhitā rajanīyā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five destinations:

english.author: sujato
english.text: hell, the animal realm, the ghost realm, humanity, and the gods.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five kinds of stinginess:

english.author: sujato
english.text: stinginess with dwellings, families, material things, praise, and the teachings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five hindrances:

english.author: sujato
english.text: sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five lower fetters:

english.author: sujato
english.text: substantialist view, doubt, misapprehension of precepts and observances, sensual desire, and ill will.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five higher fetters:

english.author: sujato
english.text: desire for rebirth in the realm of luminous form, desire for rebirth in the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five precepts:

segments.pali: pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five things that can’t be done:

segments.pali: Abhabbo, āvuso, khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṁ jīvitā voropetuṁ. Abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyituṁ. Abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu methunaṁ dhammaṁ paṭisevituṁ. Abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sampajānamusā bhāsituṁ. Abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṁ kāme paribhuñjituṁ, seyyathāpi pubbe āgārikabhūto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant with defilements ended can’t deliberately take the life of a living creature, take something with the intention to steal, have sex, tell a deliberate lie, or store up goods for their own enjoyment like they used to as a layperson.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five losses:

english.author: sujato
english.text: loss of relatives, wealth, health, ethics, and view.

segments.pali: Nāvuso, sattā ñātibyasanahetu vā bhogabyasanahetu vā rogabyasanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It is not because of loss of relatives, wealth, or health that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segments.pali: Sīlabyasanahetu vā, āvuso, sattā diṭṭhibyasanahetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It is because of loss of ethics or view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five endowments:

english.author: sujato
english.text: endowment with relatives, wealth, health, ethics, and view.

segments.pali: Nāvuso, sattā ñātisampadāhetu vā bhogasampadāhetu vā ārogyasampadāhetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It is not because of endowment with family, wealth, or health that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segments.pali: Sīlasampadāhetu vā, āvuso, sattā diṭṭhisampadāhetu vā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It is because of endowment with ethics or view that sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five drawbacks for an unethical person because of their failure in ethics:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, dussīlo sīlavipanno pamādādhikaraṇaṁ mahatiṁ bhogajāniṁ nigacchati,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, an unethical person loses great wealth on account of negligence.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first drawback.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an unethical person gets a bad reputation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second drawback.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, dussīlo sīlavipanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati yadi khattiyaparisaṁ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ yadi gahapatiparisaṁ yadi samaṇaparisaṁ, avisārado upasaṅkamati maṅkubhūto,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an unethical person enters any kind of assembly timid and embarrassed, whether it’s an assembly of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, or ascetics.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third drawback.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, dussīlo sīlavipanno sammūḷho kālaṁ karoti,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an unethical person feels lost when they die.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth drawback.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, dussīlo sīlavipanno kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an unethical person, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth drawback.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five benefits for an ethical person because of their accomplishment in ethics:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, sīlavā sīlasampanno appamādādhikaraṇaṁ mahantaṁ bhogakkhandhaṁ adhigacchati,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, an ethical person gains great wealth on account of diligence.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first benefit.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, sīlavato sīlasampannassa kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an ethical person gets a good reputation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second benefit.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, sīlavā sīlasampanno yaññadeva parisaṁ upasaṅkamati yadi khattiyaparisaṁ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṁ yadi gahapatiparisaṁ yadi samaṇaparisaṁ, visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an ethical person enters any kind of assembly bold and self-assured, whether it’s an assembly of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, or ascetics.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third benefit.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, sīlavā sīlasampanno asammūḷho kālaṁ karoti,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, an ethical person dies not feeling lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth benefit.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, sīlavā sīlasampanno kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, when an ethical person’s body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth benefit.

segments.pali: Codakena, āvuso, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhapetvā paro codetabbo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant who wants to accuse another should first establish five things in themselves:

english.author: sujato
english.text: I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time.

english.author: sujato
english.text: I will speak truthfully, not falsely.

english.author: sujato
english.text: I will speak gently, not harshly.

english.author: sujato
english.text: I will speak beneficially, not harmfully.

english.author: sujato
english.text: I will speak lovingly, not from secret hate.

segments.pali: Codakena, āvuso, bhikkhunā paraṁ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṁ upaṭṭhapetvā paro codetabbo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant who wants to accuse another should first establish these five things in themselves.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five factors that support meditation:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segments.pali: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato, lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segments.pali: Appābādho hoti appātaṅko, samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They are rarely ill or unwell. Their stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

segments.pali: Asaṭho hoti amāyāvī, yathābhūtaṁ attānaṁ āvikattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re not devious or deceitful. They reveal themselves honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

segments.pali: Āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segments.pali: Paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five pure abodes:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Aviha, Atappa, the gods fair to see, the fair seeing gods, and Akaniṭṭha.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five non-returners:

english.author: sujato
english.text: one who is extinguished between one life and the next, one who is extinguished upon landing, one who is extinguished without extra effort, one who is extinguished with extra effort, and one who heads upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five kinds of hard-heartedness:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ paṭhamo cetokhilo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving. This is the first kind of hard-heartedness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati vicikicchati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has doubts about the teaching …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the Saṅgha …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the training …

segments.pali: sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant is angry and upset with their spiritual companions, resentful and closed off.

segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, ayaṁ pañcamo cetokhilo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving. This is the fifth kind of hard-heartedness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five shackles of the heart:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant isn’t free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.

segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.
Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first shackle of the heart.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu kāye avītarāgo hoti …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant isn’t free of greed for the body …

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re not free of greed for form …

segments.pali: puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāvadatthaṁ udarāvadehakaṁ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṁ passasukhaṁ middhasukhaṁ anuyutto viharati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: They eat as much as they like until their bellies are full, then indulge in the pleasures of sleeping, lying down, and drowsing …

segments.pali: puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṁ carati: ‘imināhaṁ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lead the spiritual life hoping to be reborn in one of the orders of gods, thinking: ‘By this precept or observance or fervent austerity or spiritual practice, may I become one of the gods!’
