segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṁ carati: ‘imināhaṁ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth shackle of the heart.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five faculties:

english.author: sujato
english.text: eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another five faculties:

english.author: sujato
english.text: pleasure, pain, happiness, sadness, and equanimity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Another five faculties:

english.author: sujato
english.text: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five elements of escape:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāme manasikaroto kāmesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on sensual pleasures, but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segments.pali: Nekkhammaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on renunciation, on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segments.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ kāmehi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from sensual pleasures.

segments.pali: Ye ca kāmapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of sensual pleasures, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is how the escape from sensual pleasures is explained.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno byāpādaṁ manasikaroto byāpāde cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on ill will, but their mind does not leap forth …

segments.pali: Abyāpādaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto abyāpāde cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on good will, their mind leaps forth …

segments.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ byāpādena.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from ill will.

segments.pali: Ye ca byāpādapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ill will, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is how the escape from ill will is explained.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno vihesaṁ manasikaroto vihesāya cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on harming, but their mind does not leap forth …

segments.pali: Avihesaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto avihesāya cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on compassion, their mind leaps forth …

segments.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ vihesāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from harming.

segments.pali: Ye ca vihesāpaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of harming, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is how the escape from harming is explained.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno rūpe manasikaroto rūpesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on form, but their mind does not leap forth …

segments.pali: Arūpaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto arūpe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on the formless, their mind leaps forth …

segments.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ rūpehi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from forms.

segments.pali: Ye ca rūpapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of form, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is how the escape from forms is explained.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno sakkāyaṁ manasikaroto sakkāye cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on substantial reality, but their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segments.pali: Sakkāyanirodhaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on the cessation of substantial reality, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segments.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ sakkāyena.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from substantial reality.

segments.pali: Ye ca sakkāyapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of substantial reality, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is how the escape from substantial reality is explained.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five opportunities for freedom:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṁ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant.

segments.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṁ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthapaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches it.

segments.pali: Tassa atthapaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first opportunity for freedom.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno na heva kho satthā dhammaṁ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī, api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant. But the mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it. …

segments.pali: api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena sajjhāyaṁ karoti …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or the mendicant rehearses the teaching in detail as they learned and memorized it. …

segments.pali: api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or the mendicant thinks about and considers the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it. …

segments.pali: api ca khvassa aññataraṁ samādhinimittaṁ suggahitaṁ hoti sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritaṁ suppaṭividdhaṁ paññāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Or a meditation subject as a basis of immersion is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom.

segments.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhuno aññataraṁ samādhinimittaṁ suggahitaṁ hoti sumanasikataṁ sūpadhāritaṁ suppaṭividdhaṁ paññāya tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthapaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how a meditation subject as a basis of immersion is properly grasped, focused on, borne in mind, and penetrated with wisdom.

segments.pali: Tassa atthapaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth opportunity for freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five perceptions that ripen in freedom:

segments.pali: aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, and the perception of fading away.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena pañca dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by five that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 6. Sixes

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cha dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by six that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by six?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six interior sense fields:

segments.pali: cakkhāyatanaṁ, sotāyatanaṁ, ghānāyatanaṁ, jivhāyatanaṁ, kāyāyatanaṁ, manāyatanaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six exterior sense fields:

segments.pali: rūpāyatanaṁ, saddāyatanaṁ, gandhāyatanaṁ, rasāyatanaṁ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṁ, dhammāyatanaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six classes of consciousness:

segments.pali: cakkhuviññāṇaṁ, sotaviññāṇaṁ, ghānaviññāṇaṁ, jivhāviññāṇaṁ, kāyaviññāṇaṁ, manoviññāṇaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six classes of contact:

segments.pali: cakkhusamphasso, sotasamphasso, ghānasamphasso, jivhāsamphasso, kāyasamphasso, manosamphasso.

english.author: sujato
english.text: contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six classes of feeling:

segments.pali: cakkhusamphassajā vedanā, sotasamphassajā vedanā, ghānasamphassajā vedanā, jivhāsamphassajā vedanā, kāyasamphassajā vedanā, manosamphassajā vedanā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: feeling born of contact through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six classes of perception:

segments.pali: rūpasaññā, saddasaññā, gandhasaññā, rasasaññā, phoṭṭhabbasaññā, dhammasaññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: perceptions of sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six bodies of intention:

segments.pali: rūpasañcetanā, saddasañcetanā, gandhasañcetanā, rasasañcetanā, phoṭṭhabbasañcetanā, dhammasañcetanā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: intention regarding sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six classes of craving:

segments.pali: rūpataṇhā, saddataṇhā, gandhataṇhā, rasataṇhā, phoṭṭhabbataṇhā, dhammataṇhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: craving for sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches, and ideas.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six kinds of disrespect:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso; dhamme agāravo viharati appatisso; saṅghe agāravo viharati appatisso; sikkhāya agāravo viharati appatisso; appamāde agāravo viharati appatisso; paṭisanthāre agāravo viharati appatisso.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six kinds of respect:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari sagāravo viharati sappatisso; dhamme sagāravo viharati sappatisso; saṅghe sagāravo viharati sappatisso; sikkhāya sagāravo viharati sappatisso; appamāde sagāravo viharati sappatisso; paṭisanthāre sagāravo viharati sappatisso.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, the training, diligence, and hospitality.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six preoccupations with happiness:

segments.pali: Cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā somanassaṭṭhāniyaṁ rūpaṁ upavicarati;

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seeing a sight with the eye, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for happiness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Hearing a sound with the ear …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Smelling an odor with the nose …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Tasting a flavor with the tongue …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Encountering a touch with the body …

segments.pali: Manasā dhammaṁ viññāya somanassaṭṭhāniyaṁ dhammaṁ upavicarati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with the mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for happiness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six preoccupations with sadness:

segments.pali: Cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā domanassaṭṭhāniyaṁ rūpaṁ upavicarati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seeing a sight with the eye, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for sadness. …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya domanassaṭṭhāniyaṁ dhammaṁ upavicarati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with the mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for sadness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six preoccupations with equanimity:

segments.pali: Cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā upekkhāṭṭhāniyaṁ rūpaṁ upavicarati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seeing a sight with the eye, one is preoccupied with a sight that’s a basis for equanimity. …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya upekkhāṭṭhāniyaṁ dhammaṁ upavicarati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with the mind, one is preoccupied with an idea that’s a basis for equanimity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six warm-hearted qualities:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private.

segments.pali: Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness, both in public and in private.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ manokammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness, both in public and in private.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi, tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī hoti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni, tathārūpesu sīlesu sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a warm-hearted quality.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāyaṁ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya, tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They live according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and brings one who practices it to the complete ending of suffering.

segments.pali: Ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This warm-hearted quality too makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six roots of dispute:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant is irritable and acrimonious.

segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu kodhano hoti upanāhī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Such a mendicant lacks respect and reverence for the Teacher, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, and they don’t fulfill the training.

segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso, dhamme agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghe agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāya na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe vivādaṁ janeti. Yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They create a dispute in the Saṅgha, which is for the detriment and suffering of the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segments.pali: Evarūpañce tumhe, āvuso, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, āvuso, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha.

english.author: sujato
english.text: If you see such a root of dispute in yourselves or others, you should try to give up this bad thing.

segments.pali: Evarūpañce tumhe, āvuso, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, āvuso, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha.

english.author: sujato
english.text: If you don’t see it, you should practice so that it doesn’t come up in the future.

segments.pali: Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṁ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavo hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how to give up this bad root of dispute, so it doesn’t come up in the future.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu makkhī hoti paḷāsī …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is offensive and contemptuous …

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re jealous and stingy …

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re devious and deceitful …

english.author: sujato
english.text: They have corrupt wishes and wrong view …

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re attached to their own views, holding them tight, and refusing to let go.

segments.pali: yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī, so sattharipi agāravo viharati appatisso, dhammepi agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghepi agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāyapi na paripūrakārī hoti.

Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu satthari agāravo viharati appatisso, dhamme agāravo viharati appatisso, saṅghe agāravo viharati appatisso, sikkhāya na paripūrakārī, so saṅghe vivādaṁ janeti. Yo hoti vivādo bahujanāhitāya bahujanāsukhāya anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
Evarūpañce tumhe, āvuso, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, āvuso, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānāya vāyameyyātha.

english.author: sujato
english.text: If you see such a root of dispute in yourselves or others, you should try to give up this bad thing.

segments.pali: Evarūpañce tumhe, āvuso, vivādamūlaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā na samanupasseyyātha. Tatra tumhe, āvuso, tasseva pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavāya paṭipajjeyyātha.

english.author: sujato
english.text: If you don’t see it, you should practice so that it doesn’t come up in the future.

segments.pali: Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa pahānaṁ hoti. Evametassa pāpakassa vivādamūlassa āyatiṁ anavassavo hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how to give up this bad root of dispute, so it doesn’t come up in the future.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six elements:

segments.pali: pathavīdhātu, āpodhātu, tejodhātu, vāyodhātu, ākāsadhātu, viññāṇadhātu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: earth, water, fire, air, space, and consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six elements of escape:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take a mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘mettā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā,

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by love. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segments.pali: atha ca pana me byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow ill will still occupies my mind.’

segments.pali: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo, ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso, yaṁ mettāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the heart’s release by love has been developed and properly implemented,

segments.pali: Atha ca panassa byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: yet somehow ill will still occupies the mind.

segments.pali: Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, byāpādassa, yadidaṁ mettā cetovimuttī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the heart’s release by love that is the escape from ill will.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘karuṇā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by compassion. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segments.pali: Atha ca pana me vihesā cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow the thought of harming still occupies my mind.’

segments.pali: so ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso, yaṁ karuṇāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya,
atha ca panassa vihesā cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, vihesāya, yadidaṁ karuṇā cetovimuttī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the heart’s release by compassion that is the escape from thoughts of harming.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘muditā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by rejoicing. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segments.pali: Atha ca pana me arati cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow discontent still occupies my mind.’

segments.pali: so ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso, yaṁ muditāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya,
atha ca panassa arati cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, aratiyā, yadidaṁ muditā cetovimuttī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the heart’s release by rejoicing that is the escape from discontent.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘upekkhā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by equanimity. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segments.pali: Atha ca pana me rāgo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow desire still occupies my mind.’

segments.pali: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso, yaṁ upekkhāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya,
atha ca panassa rāgo cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, rāgassa, yadidaṁ upekkhā cetovimuttī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the heart’s release by equanimity that is the escape from desire.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘animittā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve developed the signless release of the heart. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segments.pali: Atha ca pana me nimittānusāri viññāṇaṁ hotī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow my consciousness still follows after signs.’

segments.pali: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! …

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso, yaṁ animittāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya,
atha ca panassa nimittānusāri viññāṇaṁ bhavissati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, sabbanimittānaṁ, yadidaṁ animittā cetovimuttī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the signless release of the heart that is the escape from all signs.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take another mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘asmīti kho me vigataṁ, ayamahamasmīti na samanupassāmi,

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’m rid of the conceit “I am”. And I don’t regard anything as “I am this”.

segments.pali: atha ca pana me vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupies my mind.’

segments.pali: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi, na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, āvuso, anavakāso, yaṁ asmīti vigate ayamahamasmīti asamanupassato,

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the conceit “I am” has been done away with, and nothing is regarded as “I am this”,

segments.pali: atha ca panassa vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallaṁ cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassati, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: yet somehow the dart of doubt and indecision still occupy the mind.

segments.pali: Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, vicikicchākathaṅkathāsallassa, yadidaṁ asmimānasamugghāto’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the uprooting of the conceit “I am” that is the escape from the dart of doubt and indecision.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six unsurpassable things:

segments.pali: dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ, anussatānuttariyaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six topics for recollection:

segments.pali: buddhānussati, dhammānussati, saṅghānussati, sīlānussati, cāgānussati, devatānussati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the recollection of the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, ethics, generosity, and the deities.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six consistent responses:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Hearing a sound with their ears … Smelling an odor with their nose … Tasting a flavor with their tongue … Encountering a touch with their body …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six classes of rebirth:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco kaṇhābhijātiko samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to a dark result.

segments.pali: Idha panāvuso, ekacco kaṇhābhijātiko samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to a bright result.

segments.pali: Idha panāvuso, ekacco kaṇhābhijātiko samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone born into a dark class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

segments.pali: Idha panāvuso, ekacco sukkābhijātiko samāno sukkaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to a bright result.

segments.pali: Idha panāvuso, ekacco sukkābhijātiko samāno kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ abhijāyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to a dark result.

segments.pali: Idha panāvuso, ekacco sukkābhijātiko samāno akaṇhaṁ asukkaṁ nibbānaṁ abhijāyati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone born into a bright class gives rise to extinguishment, which is neither dark nor bright.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six perceptions that help penetration:

segments.pali: aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cha dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by six that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 7. Sevens

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena satta dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by seven that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by seven?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven riches of the noble ones:

segments.pali: saddhādhanaṁ, sīladhanaṁ, hiridhanaṁ, ottappadhanaṁ, sutadhanaṁ, cāgadhanaṁ, paññādhanaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the riches of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven awakening factors:

segments.pali: satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven prerequisites for immersion:

segments.pali: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, and right mindfulness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven bad qualities:

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, appassuto hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, duppañño hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, unlearned, lazy, unmindful, and witless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven good qualities:

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, paññavā hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, energetic, mindful, and wise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven aspects of the teachings of the true persons:

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu dhammaññū ca hoti atthaññū ca attaññū ca mattaññū ca kālaññū ca parisaññū ca puggalaññū ca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a mendicant knows the teachings, knows the meaning, knows themselves, knows moderation, knows the right time, knows assemblies, and knows individuals.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven qualifications for graduation:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sikkhāsamādāne tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca sikkhāsamādāne avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has a keen enthusiasm to undertake the training …

segments.pali: Dhammanisantiyā tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca dhammanisantiyā avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to examine the teachings …

segments.pali: Icchāvinaye tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca icchāvinaye avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to get rid of desires …

segments.pali: Paṭisallāne tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca paṭisallāne avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: for retreat …

segments.pali: Vīriyārambhe tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca vīriyārambhe avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to rouse up energy …

segments.pali: Satinepakke tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca satinepakke avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: for mindfulness and alertness …

segments.pali: Diṭṭhipaṭivedhe tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca diṭṭhipaṭivedhe avigatapemo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to penetrate theoretically. And they don’t lose these desires in the future.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven perceptions:

segments.pali: aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, asubhasaññā, ādīnavasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of ugliness, the perception of drawbacks, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven powers:

segments.pali: saddhābalaṁ, vīriyabalaṁ, hiribalaṁ, ottappabalaṁ, satibalaṁ, samādhibalaṁ, paññābalaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: faith, energy, conscience, prudence, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven planes of consciousness:

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of streaming radiance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh plane of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven individuals worthy of a religious donation:

segments.pali: ubhatobhāgavimutto, paññāvimutto, kāyasakkhi, diṭṭhippatto, saddhāvimutto, dhammānusārī, saddhānusārī.

english.author: sujato
english.text: one freed both ways, one freed by wisdom, a direct witness, one attained to view, one freed by faith, a follower of teachings, and a follower by faith.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven underlying tendencies:

segments.pali: kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo, mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven fetters:

segments.pali: anunayasaṁyojanaṁ, paṭighasaṁyojanaṁ, diṭṭhisaṁyojanaṁ, vicikicchāsaṁyojanaṁ, mānasaṁyojanaṁ, bhavarāgasaṁyojanaṁ, avijjāsaṁyojanaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: attraction, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.

segments.pali: Satta adhikaraṇasamathā uppannuppannānaṁ adhikaraṇānaṁ samathāya vūpasamāya—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven principles for the settlement of any disciplinary issues that might arise:

segments.pali: sammukhāvinayo dātabbo, sativinayo dātabbo, amūḷhavinayo dātabbo, paṭiññāya kāretabbaṁ, yebhuyyasikā, tassapāpiyasikā, tiṇavatthārako.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Resolution face-to-face to be applied. Resolution through recollection to be granted. Resolution because of past insanity to be granted. Acting according to what has been admitted. Majority decision. Further penalty. Covering over as if with grass.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena satta dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by seven that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The second recitation section is complete.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 8. Eights

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena aṭṭha dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by eight that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by eight?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight wrong ways:

segments.pali: micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo micchāsati, micchāsamādhi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight right ways:

segments.pali: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight individuals worthy of a religious donation:

segments.pali: sotāpanno, sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno; sakadāgāmī, sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno; anāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno; arahā, arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The stream-enterer and the one practicing to realize the fruit of stream-entry. The once-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of once-return. The non-returner and the one practicing to realize the fruit of non-return. The perfected one, and the one practicing for perfection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight grounds for laziness:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘kammaṁ kho me kātabbaṁ bhavissati, kammaṁ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilamissati, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I have some work to do. But while doing it my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

segments.pali: So nipajjati na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā kammaṁ kataṁ hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho kammaṁ akāsiṁ, kammaṁ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilanto, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve done some work. But while working my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gantabbo hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘maggo kho me gantabbo bhavissati, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilamissati, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I have to go on a journey. But while walking my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gato hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho maggaṁ agamāsiṁ, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilanto, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. But while walking my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto na labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, but they didn’t get to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto nālatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo kilanto akammañño, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, but I didn’t get to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is tired and unfit for work. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, and they got to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto alatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo garuko akammañño, māsācitaṁ maññe, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, and I got to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is heavy and unfit for work, like I’ve just eaten a load of beans. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno uppanno hoti appamattako ābādho.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant feels a little sick.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I feel a little sick. Lying down would be good for me. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gilānā vuṭṭhito hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has recently recovered from illness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gilānā vuṭṭhito aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā, tassa me kāyo dubbalo akammañño, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve recently recovered from illness. My body is weak and unfit for work. I’d better have a lie down.’

segments.pali: So nipajjati na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth ground for laziness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight grounds for arousing energy:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘kammaṁ kho me kātabbaṁ bhavissati, kammaṁ kho pana me karontena na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I have some work to do. While working it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segments.pali: So vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā kammaṁ kataṁ hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho kammaṁ akāsiṁ, kammaṁ kho panāhaṁ karonto nāsakkhiṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve done some work. While I was working I wasn’t able to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse up energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gantabbo hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘maggo kho me gantabbo bhavissati, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantena na sukaraṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I have to go on a journey. While walking it’s not easy to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse up energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gato hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho maggaṁ agamāsiṁ, maggaṁ kho panāhaṁ gacchanto nāsakkhiṁ buddhānaṁ sāsanaṁ manasi kātuṁ, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. While I was walking I wasn’t able to focus on the instructions of the Buddhas. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse up energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto na labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, but they didn’t get to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto nālatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo lahuko kammañño, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, but I didn’t get to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is light and fit for work. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse up energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto labhati lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has wandered for alms, and they got to fill up on as much food as they like, coarse or fine.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya caranto alatthaṁ lūkhassa vā paṇītassa vā bhojanassa yāvadatthaṁ pāripūriṁ, tassa me kāyo balavā kammañño, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve wandered for alms, and I got to fill up on as much food as I like, coarse or fine. My body is strong and fit for work. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse up energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno uppanno hoti appamattako ābādho.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant feels a little sick.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘uppanno kho me ayaṁ appamattako ābādho, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me ābādho pavaḍḍheyya, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I feel a little sick. It’s possible this illness will worsen. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse up energy…

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh ground for arousing energy.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu gilānā vuṭṭhito hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has recently recovered from illness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho gilānā vuṭṭhito aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā, ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ vijjati yaṁ me ābādho paccudāvatteyya, handāhaṁ vīriyaṁ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve recently recovered from illness. It’s possible the illness will come back. I’d better preemptively rouse up energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.’

segments.pali: So vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth ground for arousing energy.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight reasons to give:

segments.pali: Āsajja dānaṁ deti, bhayā dānaṁ deti, ‘adāsi me’ti dānaṁ deti, ‘dassati me’ti dānaṁ deti, ‘sāhu dānan’ti dānaṁ deti, ‘ahaṁ pacāmi, ime na pacanti, nārahāmi pacanto apacantānaṁ dānaṁ na dātun’ti dānaṁ deti, ‘idaṁ me dānaṁ dadato kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchatī’ti dānaṁ deti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone might give a gift after insulting the recipient. Or they give out of fear. Or they give thinking, ‘They gave to me.’ Or they give thinking, ‘They’ll give to me.’ Or they give thinking, ‘It’s good to give.’ Or they give thinking, ‘I cook, they don’t. It wouldn’t be right for me to not give to them.’ Or they give thinking, ‘By giving this gift I’ll get a good reputation.’ Or they give thinking, ‘This is an adornment and requisite for the mind.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight rebirths by giving:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, ekacco dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: First, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Whatever they give they expect back.

segments.pali: So passati khattiyamahāsālaṁ vā brāhmaṇamahāsālaṁ vā gahapatimahāsālaṁ vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitaṁ samaṅgībhūtaṁ paricārayamānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They see an affluent aristocrat or brahmin or householder amusing themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṁ vā brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṁ vā gahapatimahāsālānaṁ vā sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of well-to-do aristocrats or brahmins or householders!’

segments.pali: So taṁ cittaṁ dahati, taṁ cittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, taṁ cittaṁ bhāveti, tassa taṁ cittaṁ hīne vimuttaṁ uttari abhāvitaṁ tatrūpapattiyā saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They settle on that thought, stabilize it, and develop it. As they’ve settled for less and not developed further, their thought leads to rebirth there.

segments.pali: Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi no dussīlassa.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their purity.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, idhekacco dānaṁ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ …pe… seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Next, someone gives to ascetics or brahmins.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Whatever they give they expect back.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And they’ve heard:

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘The gods of the four great kings are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.

english.text: ‘The gods of the thirty-three …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the gods of Yama …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the joyful gods …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the gods who love to create …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the gods who control what is created by others are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others!’
