english.text: But I say that this is only for those of ethical conduct, not for the unethical.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And for those free of desire, not those with desire.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The heart’s wish of an ethical person succeeds because of their freedom from desire.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight assemblies:

segments.pali: khattiyaparisā, brāhmaṇaparisā, gahapatiparisā, samaṇaparisā, cātumahārājikaparisā, tāvatiṁsaparisā, māraparisā, brahmaparisā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the assemblies of aristocrats, brahmins, householders, and ascetics. An assembly of the gods of the four great kings. An assembly of the gods of the thirty-three. An assembly of Māras. An assembly of divinities.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight worldly conditions:

segments.pali: lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṁsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañca.

english.author: sujato
english.text: gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight dimensions of mastery:

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṁ nīlaṁ nīlavaṇṇaṁ nīlanidassanaṁ nīlanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ nīlaṁ nīlavaṇṇaṁ nīlanidassanaṁ nīlanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like a flax flower that’s blue, with blue color and blue appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṁ pītaṁ pītavaṇṇaṁ pītanidassanaṁ pītanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ pītaṁ pītavaṇṇaṁ pītanidassanaṁ pītanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like a champak flower that’s yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are red, with red color and red appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṁ lohitakaṁ lohitakavaṇṇaṁ lohitakanidassanaṁ lohitakanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ lohitakaṁ lohitakavaṇṇaṁ lohitakanidassanaṁ lohitakanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like a scarlet mallow flower that’s red, with red color and red appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, red, with red color and red appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are white, with white color and white appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ odātaṁ odātavaṇṇaṁ odātanidassanaṁ odātanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like the morning star that’s white, with white color and white appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, white, with white color and white appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth dimension of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight liberations:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Having physical form, they see forms.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving physical form internally, they see forms externally.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re focused only on beauty.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth liberation.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena aṭṭha dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by eight that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 9. Nines

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena nava dhammā sammadakkhātā;

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by nine that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by nine?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine grounds for resentment:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me,’ you harbor resentment.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong to me’ …

segments.pali: ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṁ acarī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They did wrong by someone I love’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are doing wrong by someone I love’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong by someone I love’ …

segments.pali: ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṁ acarī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati …pe…

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They helped someone I dislike’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are helping someone I dislike’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike,’ you harbor resentment.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine ways to get rid of resentment:

segments.pali: ‘Anatthaṁ me acari, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

segments.pali: ‘anatthaṁ me carati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me …’ …

segments.pali: ‘anatthaṁ me carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong to me …’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They did wrong by someone I love …’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are doing wrong by someone I love …’ …

segments.pali: anatthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong by someone I love …’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They helped someone I dislike …’ …

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are helping someone I dislike …’ …

segments.pali: atthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine abodes of sentient beings:

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of streaming radiance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā asaññino appaṭisaṁvedino, seyyathāpi devā asaññasattā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are non-percipient and do not experience anything, such as the gods who are non-percipient beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of nothingness. They have been reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the ninth abode of sentient beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine lost opportunities for spiritual practice:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, tathāgato ca loke uppanno hoti arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a Realized One has arisen in the world. He teaches the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But that individual has been reborn in hell.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, tathāgato ca loke uppanno hoti arahaṁ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But that individual has been reborn in the animal realm.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But an individual has been reborn in the ghost realm.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But that individual has been reborn among the titans.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But that individual has been reborn in one of the long-lived orders of gods.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

segments.pali: paccantimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti milakkhesu aviññātāresu, yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ upāsakānaṁ upāsikānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But that individual has been reborn in the borderlands, among uneducated foreigners, where monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen do not go.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

segments.pali: majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti. So ca hoti micchādiṭṭhiko viparītadassano:

english.author: sujato
english.text: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they have wrong view and distorted perspective:

segments.pali: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ, natthi hutaṁ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, natthi ayaṁ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a Realized One has arisen in the world.

segments.pali: majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti. So ca hoti duppañño jaḷo eḷamūgo, nappaṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they’re witless, dull, idiotic, and unable to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, tathāgato ca loke na uppanno hoti arahaṁ sammāsambuddho,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, no Realized One has arisen in the world,

segments.pali: dhammo ca na desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito. Ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti paññavā ajaḷo aneḷamūgo, paṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: so there is no teaching of the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One. But an individual is reborn in a central country. And they’re wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the ninth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine progressive meditations:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segments.pali: Vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segments.pali: Pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, personally experiencing the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

segments.pali: Sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā …pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segments.pali: Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine progressive cessations:

segments.pali: Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa kāmasaññā niruddhā hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the first absorption, sensual perceptions have ceased.

segments.pali: Dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā niruddhā honti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the second absorption, the placing of the mind and keeping it connected have ceased.

segments.pali: Tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa pīti niruddhā hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the third absorption, rapture has ceased.

segments.pali: Catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa assāsapassāssā niruddhā honti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the fourth absorption, breathing has ceased.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite space, the perception of form has ceased.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite consciousness, the perception of the dimension of infinite space has ceased.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of nothingness, the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness has ceased.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, the perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased.

segments.pali: Saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca niruddhā honti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena nava dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: These are the teachings grouped by nine that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: 10. Tens

segments.pali: Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dasa dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are teachings grouped by ten that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ …pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert.

english.author: sujato
english.text: What are the teachings grouped by ten?

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten qualities that serve as protector:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti. Pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati, ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti …pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is easy to admonish, having qualities that make them easy to admonish. They’re patient, and take instruction respectfully.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu suvaco hoti …pe… padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṁ uccāvacāni kiṅkaraṇīyāni, tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgato, alaṁ kātuṁ alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is deft and tireless in a diverse spectrum of duties for their spiritual companions, understanding how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṁ …pe… alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant loves the teachings and is a delight to converse with, being full of joy in the teaching and training.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarehi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati …pe… anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti …pe… saritā anussaritā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten universal dimensions of meditation:

segments.pali: Pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti, uddhaṁ adho tiriyaṁ advayaṁ appamāṇaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone perceives the meditation on universal earth above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They perceive the meditation on universal water …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal fire …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal air …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal blue …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal yellow …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal red …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal white …

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal space …

segments.pali: viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti, uddhaṁ adho tiriyaṁ advayaṁ appamāṇaṁ.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They perceive the meditation on universal consciousness above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten ways of doing unskillful deeds:

segments.pali: pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṁ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten ways of doing skillful deeds:

segments.pali: pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi.

english.author: sujato
english.text: refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; refraining from speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten abodes of the noble ones:

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti, chaḷaṅgasamannāgato, ekārakkho, caturāpasseno, paṇunnapaccekasacco, samavayasaṭṭhesano, anāvilasaṅkappo, passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro, suvimuttacitto, suvimuttapañño.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has given up five factors, possesses six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth, has totally given up searching, has unsullied intentions, has stilled the physical process, and is well freed in mind and well freed by wisdom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant given up five factors?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant has given up sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has given up five factors.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant possess six factors?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Hearing a sound with their ears … Smelling an odor with their nose … Tasting a flavor with their tongue … Encountering a touch with their body …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu chaḷaṅgasamannāgato hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant possesses six factors.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant have a single guard?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satārakkhena cetasā samannāgato hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant’s heart is guarded by mindfulness.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu ekārakkho hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has a single guard.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant have four supports?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṁ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṁ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṁ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṁ vinodeti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: After appraisal, a mendicant uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and gets rid of some things.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu caturāpasseno hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has four supports.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno yāni tāni puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ puthupaccekasaccāni, sabbāni tāni nunnāni honti paṇunnāni cattāni vantāni muttāni pahīnāni paṭinissaṭṭhāni.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Different ascetics and brahmins have different idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth. A mendicant has cast out, cast aside, thrown out, discarded, let go of, given up, and relinquished all these.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu paṇunnapaccekasacco hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant totally given up searching?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmesanā pahīnā hoti, bhavesanā pahīnā hoti, brahmacariyesanā paṭippassaddhā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when they’ve given up searching for sensual pleasures, for continued existence, and for a spiritual path.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu samavayasaṭṭhesano hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has totally given up searching.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant have unsullied intentions?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, byāpādasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, vihiṁsāsaṅkappo pahīno hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when they’ve given up sensual, malicious, and cruel intentions.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu anāvilasaṅkappo hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has unsullied intentions.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant stilled the physical process?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has stilled the physical process.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how is a mendicant well freed in mind?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno rāgā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, dosā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, mohā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant’s mind is freed from greed, hate, and delusion.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttacitto hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant is well freed in mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how is a mendicant well freed by wisdom?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘rāgo me pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant understands: ‘I’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.’

segments.pali: ‘Doso me pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti.
‘Moho me pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti.
Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttapañño hoti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant’s mind is well freed by wisdom.

english.author: sujato

english.author: sujato
english.text: an adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

segments.pali: Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dasa dhammā sammadakkhātā.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Reverends, these are the teachings grouped by ten that have been rightly explained by the Buddha.

segments.pali: Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṁ na vivaditabbaṁ, yathayidaṁ brahmacariyaṁ addhaniyaṁ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṁ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: You should all recite these in concert, without disputing, so that this spiritual path may last for a long time. That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

segments.pali: Atha kho bhagavā uṭṭhahitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ āmantesi:

english.author: sujato

english.author: sujato
english.text: “Good, good, Sāriputta!

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s good that you’ve taught this exposition of the reciting in concert.”

english.author: sujato
english.text: That is what Venerable Sāriputta said, and the teacher approved.

segments.pali: Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what Sāriputta said.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are five things that are of great help; five things that are to be cultivated; five things that are to be understood accurately; five things that are to be abandoned; five things that lead to backsliding; five things that lead to accomplishment; five things that are hard to penetrate; five things that are to be encouraged; five things that are to be understood fully; five things that are to be seen for oneself.

english.text: What are the five things that are of great help?

english.text: What five things are helpful?

english.text: The five constituents of exertion—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five factors that support meditation.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has faith and is confident in the enlightenment of the Such-Attained One:

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segments.pali: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘He is thus the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Fully Enlightened Buddha. He is accomplished in knowledge and conduct; the Well Gone One; knower of worlds. He is the unsurpassed coachman of trainable people; the Teacher of angels and humans. He is the Buddha, the Blessed One.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segments.pali: Appābādho hoti appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He is healthy, has few ailments, and has good digestion which is neither too cold nor too hot but is moderate and fit for exertion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They are rarely ill or unwell. Their stomach digests well, being neither too hot nor too cold, but just right, and fit for meditation.

segments.pali: Asaṭho hoti amāyāvī yathābhūtamattānaṁ āvīkattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: They are honest, guileless, and open themselves up as they are to the teacher or their knowledgeable fellows in the holy life.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re not devious or deceitful. They reveal themselves honestly to the Teacher or sensible spiritual companions.

segments.pali: Āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He dwells with resolute energy for the purpose of abandoning unwholesome mental states and for arousing wholesome mental states. He is steadfast, firm in his exertion, and is not remiss in his responsibilities regarding wholesome mental states.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They live with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They’re strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segments.pali: Paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: They are discerning and endowed with the discernment that attends to arising and passing, that is noble, penetrative, and leads rightly to the destruction of suffering.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk doubts and is apprehensive about the teacher, and they are neither inspired nor pleased with him.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant has doubts about the Teacher. They’re uncertain, undecided, and lacking confidence.

segments.pali: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The mind of such a monk does not incline to ardor, devoted practice, perseverance, or exertion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This being so, their mind doesn’t incline toward keenness, commitment, persistence, and striving.

segments.pali: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.

english.text: For one whose mind does not incline to ardor, devoted practice, perseverance, or exertion,

segments.pali: Yassa cittaṁ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya.

english.text: For one whose mind does not incline to ardor, devoted practice, perseverance, or exertion,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The five elements leading to a way out—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five elements of escape.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāme manasikaroto kāmesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, when a monk is considering sensuality, his mind does not pursue, become satisfied with, fixate on, or find release in sensual pleasures.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant focuses on sensual pleasures, but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segments.pali: Nekkhammaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Rather, when he is considering renunciation, his mind pursues, is satisfied with, fixates on, and finds release in that instead.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on renunciation, on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segments.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ kāmehi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For him, the mind is well gone, cultivated, aroused, freed, and unyoked from sensual pleasures.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from sensual pleasures.

segments.pali: Ye ca kāmapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātā pariḷāhā, mutto so tehi. Na so taṁ vedanaṁ vedeti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And further, he is freed from the outflows, distress, and fevers that are supported by sensuality. He does not experience that feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of sensual pleasures, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is declared to be the way out of sensual pleasures.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is how the escape from sensual pleasures is explained.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno byāpādaṁ manasikaroto byāpāde cittaṁ na pakkhandati na pasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.

english.text: Moreover, when a monk is considering embodied personality, his mind does not pursue, become satisfied with, fixate on, or find release in it.

english.author: sujato

english.text: Rather, when he is considering the ending of embodied personality, his mind pursues, is satisfied with, fixates on, and finds release in the that instead.

english.author: sujato
english.text: But when they focus on the cessation of substantial reality, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The five Right Collectedness accompanied with knowledge:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Right immersion with five knowledges.

segments.pali: ‘ayaṁ samādhi paccuppannasukho ceva āyatiñca sukhavipāko’ti paccattaṁyeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The first-hand knowledge arises: ‘This collectedness is pleasant now and will also result in pleasure in the future.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: The following knowledges arise for you personally: ‘This immersion is blissful now, and results in bliss in the future.’

segments.pali: ‘Ayaṁ samādhi ariyo nirāmiso’ti paccattaññeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The first-hand knowledge arises: ‘This collectedness is noble and metaphysical.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘This immersion is noble and not of the flesh.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The first-hand knowledge arises: ‘This collectedness is associated with exceptional people.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘This immersion is not cultivated by reprobates.’

segments.pali: ‘Ayaṁ samādhi santo paṇīto paṭippassaddhaladdho ekodibhāvādhigato, na sasaṅkhāraniggayhavāritagato’ti paccattaṁyeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The first-hand knowledge arises: ‘This collectedness is peaceful, refined, gained through ready tranquility, attained through unification, and is not gotten through suppressed repressing of volitional action.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘This immersion is peaceful and sublime and tranquil and unified, not held in place by forceful suppression.’

segments.pali: ‘So kho panāhaṁ imaṁ samādhiṁ satova samāpajjāmi sato vuṭṭhahāmī’ti paccattaṁyeva ñāṇaṁ uppajjati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The first-hand knowledge arises: ‘Mindfully, I ender this collectedness and mindfully, I emerge from it.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I mindfully enter into and emerge from this immersion.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the five things that are to be encouraged.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The five strategies for freedom—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Five opportunities for freedom.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṁ deseti aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a teacher or a certain of one's fellows in the holy life in the place of a teacher teaches the Dhamma to a monk.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant.

segments.pali: Yathā yathā, āvuso, bhikkhuno satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī tathā tathā so tasmiṁ dhamme atthappaṭisaṁvedī ca hoti dhammapaṭisaṁvedī ca.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: In whatever ways a teacher or a certain of one's fellows in the holy life in the place of a teacher teach the Dhamma to that monk, in just those ways he appreciates the significance and he appreciates the methodology in that Dhamma.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That mendicant feels inspired by the meaning and the teaching in that Dhamma, no matter how the Teacher or a respected spiritual companion teaches it.

segments.pali: Tassa atthappaṭisaṁvedino dhammapaṭisaṁvedino pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who appreciates significance and methodology, gladness arises. For one who is glad, joy arises. For one of joyful mind, the body relaxes. A relaxed body experiences ease. The mind of one experiencing ease becomes collected.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Feeling inspired, joy springs up. Being joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, one feels bliss. And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first strategy for freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first opportunity for freedom.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno na heva kho satthā dhammaṁ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī, api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ vitthārena paresaṁ deseti

english.text: Or alternatively, a teacher or a certain of one's fellows in the holy life in the place of a teacher do not teach the Dhamma to a monk, but rather, he teaches the Dhamma that he has heard and studied, with explanation, to others.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, it may be that neither the Teacher nor a respected spiritual companion teaches Dhamma to a mendicant. But the mendicant teaches Dhamma in detail to others as they learned and memorized it.

english.author: sujato

english.author: sujato
english.text: 6. Groups of Six

segments.pali: Cha dhammā bahukārā …pe… cha dhammā sacchikātabbā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are six things that are of great help; six things that are to be cultivated; six things that are to be understood accurately; six things that are to be abandoned; six things that lead to backsliding; six things that lead to accomplishment; six things that are hard to penetrate; six things that are to be encouraged; six things that are to be understood fully; six things that are to be seen for oneself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six things are helpful, etc.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the six things that are of great help?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What six things are helpful?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The six qualities of graciousness to be remembered.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six warm-hearted qualities.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ kāyakammaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk's bodily action is consistently grounded in loving-kindness toward his fellows in the holy life both in public and private.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with bodily kindness, both in public and in private.

segments.pali: ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This quality of graciousness to be remembered elicits friendliness and respect, and leads to sympathy, absence of conflict, harmony, and unity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This warm-hearted quality makes for fondness and respect, conducing to inclusion, harmony, and unity, without quarreling.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ vacīkammaṁ …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk's verbal action is consistently grounded in loving kindness toward his fellows in the holy life both in public and private ... and this leads to ... unity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with verbal kindness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno mettaṁ manokammaṁ …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk's mental action is consistently grounded in loving-kindness toward his fellows in the holy life both in public and private ... and this leads to ... unity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant consistently treats their spiritual companions with mental kindness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi, tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī hoti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk is devoted to sharing whatever righteous gains he has gained rightly—even a measure of the content's of his own bowl—with his virtuous fellows in the holy life. He is devoted to this commonality. This quality of graciousness too is to be remembered ... and it leads to ... unity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl, using them in common with their ethical spiritual companions.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu, yāni tāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni, tathārūpesu sīlesu sīlasāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo …pe… ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk dwells keeping the same precepts as his fellows in the holy life both in public and private. Those precepts are kept unbroken, impeccable, unsullied, untarnished, and are consistently upheld; they are freeing, praised by knowledgeable people, and they lead to collectedness. This quality of graciousness too is to be remembered ... and it leads to ... unity.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the precepts shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. Those precepts are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāyaṁ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya, tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhi sāmaññagato viharati sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk dwells keeping the same views—noble, emancipating, and leading those who hold them to the destruction of suffering—as his fellows in the holy life both in public and private.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant lives according to the view shared with their spiritual companions, both in public and in private. That view is noble and emancipating, and delivers one who practices it to the complete ending of suffering.

segments.pali: ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo, saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṁvattati.

english.author: sujato

english.text: Here, a monk dwells disrespectful and defiant toward the teacher ... toward the Dhamma ... toward the Saṅgha ... toward the training ... toward the quality of attentiveness ... he dwells disrespectful and defiant toward the quality of hospitality.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk dwells respectfully and deferentially toward the teacher ... toward the Dhamma ... toward the Saṅgha ... toward the training ... toward the quality of attentiveness ... he dwells respectfully and deferentially toward the quality of hospitality.

english.author: sujato

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk might speak thus:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Take a mendicant who says:

segments.pali: ‘mettā hi kho me, cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Truly, I have cultivated freedom of mind through loving-kindness. I have exercised it, deeply experienced it, fortified it, and undertaken it well. I have made it my vehicle and my foundation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve developed the heart’s release by love. I’ve cultivated it, made it my vehicle and my basis, kept it up, consolidated it, and properly implemented it.

segments.pali: atha ca pana me byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: But still, ill will persists in taking hold of my mind.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Yet somehow ill will still occupies my mind.’

segments.pali: So ‘mā hevan’tissa vacanīyo ‘māyasmā evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhakkhānaṁ, na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He should be told: ‘Not so! Venerable, don't speak thus! Do not misrepresent the Blessed One. Misrepresenting the Blessed One is not good. Surely the Blessed One would not speak thus!

english.author: sujato
english.text: They should be told, ‘Not so, venerable! Don’t say that. Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.

segments.pali: Aṭṭhānametaṁ āvuso anavakāso yaṁ mettāya cetovimuttiyā bhāvitāya bahulīkatāya yānīkatāya vatthukatāya anuṭṭhitāya paricitāya susamāraddhāya.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Friend, it is not possible, there is no way, when freedom of mind through loving-kindness has been cultivated, exercised, deeply experienced, fortified, undertaken well, and when it has been made one's vehicle and one's foundation, that

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s impossible, reverend, it cannot happen that the heart’s release by love has been developed and properly implemented,

segments.pali: Atha ca panassa byāpādo cittaṁ pariyādāya ṭhassatīti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ill will could still persist in taking hold of one's mind. That is not a possibility.

english.author: sujato
english.text: yet somehow ill will still occupies the mind.

segments.pali: Nissaraṇaṁ hetaṁ, āvuso, byāpādassa, yadidaṁ mettācetovimuttī’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Indeed, friend, freedom of mind through loving-kindness is the way out of ill will.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: For it is the heart’s release by love that is the escape from ill will.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Or, here, a monk might speak thus:

english.author: sujato

segments.pali: ‘karuṇā hi kho me cetovimutti bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.
