english.text: The six stable abidings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six consistent responses.

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, friend, a monk having seen a form with the eye, is not elated nor dejected, but abides stoically composed, mindful, and integrally aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having heard a sound with the ear ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Hearing a sound with their ears …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having smelled an odor with the nose ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Smelling an odor with their nose …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having tasted a flavor with the tongue ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having felt a touch via the body ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Encountering a touch with their body …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having cognized a thought with the mind, he is not elated nor dejected, but abides stoically composed, mindful, and integrally aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the six things that are to be encouraged.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the six things that are to be understood fully?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What six things should be directly known?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The six unsurpassables—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six unsurpassable things:

segments.pali: dassanānuttariyaṁ, savanānuttariyaṁ, lābhānuttariyaṁ, sikkhānuttariyaṁ, pāricariyānuttariyaṁ, anussatānuttariyaṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Unsurpassable sight; unsurpassable sound; unsurpassable gain; unsurpassable training; unsurpassable service; unsurpassable recollection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the unsurpassable seeing, listening, acquisition, training, service, and recollection.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the six things that are to be understood fully.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the six things that are to be seen for oneself?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What six things should be realized?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The six direct knowledges—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Six direct knowledges.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu anekavihitaṁ iddhividhaṁ paccanubhoti—ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṁ tirobhāvaṁ; tirokuṭṭaṁ tiropākāraṁ tiropabbataṁ asajjamāno gacchati seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṁ karoti seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchati seyyathāpi pathaviyaṁ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamati seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṁmahiddhike evaṁmahānubhāve pāṇinā parāmasati parimajjati; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṁ vatteti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, friend, a monk acquires various psychic powers—having been one, he becomes many; have been many, he becomes one; appearing and disappearing, he moves unimpeded through walls, ramparts, and mountains as if they were empty space; he dives in and out of the earth as if it was water; he goes across water without breaking the surface as if it were earth; he travels with legs crossed through empty space as if a winged bird; he touches and strokes the powerful and majestic moon and sun with his hand; he has the power to go with the body even up to the world of the gods.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant wields the many kinds of psychic power: multiplying themselves and becoming one again; materializing and dematerializing; going unobstructed through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; diving in and out of the earth as if it were water; walking on water as if it were earth; flying cross-legged through the sky like a bird; touching and stroking with the hand the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful; controlling the body as far as the realm of divinity.

segments.pali: Dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya ubho sadde suṇāti dibbe ca mānuse ca, ye dūre santike ca.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the purification of the divine, superhuman ear element, he hears both sounds - divine and human, far and near.

english.author: sujato
english.text: With clairaudience that is purified and superhuman, they hear both kinds of sounds, human and heavenly, whether near or far.

segments.pali: Parasattānaṁ parapuggalānaṁ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He knows the mind of other beings and other people having enveloped mind with mind.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They understand the minds of other beings and individuals, having encompassed them with their own mind.

segments.pali: sarāgaṁ vā cittaṁ sarāgaṁ cittanti pajānāti …pe…

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He knows an impassioned mind as an impassioned mind ...

segments.pali: avimuttaṁ vā cittaṁ avimuttaṁ cittanti pajānāti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He knows an unfree mind as an unfree mind.

segments.pali: So anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati, seyyathidaṁ—ekampi jātiṁ …pe… iti sākāraṁ sauddesaṁ anekavihitaṁ pubbenivāsaṁ anussarati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He recollects previous existence of various assortment, namely: one former life ... Thus, he recollects previous existence of various assortment with their attributes and details.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They recollect many kinds of past lives, with features and details.

segments.pali: Dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti …pe…

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the purified, divine, superhuman eye, he sees beings dying and being reborn. And he distinguishes beings as coarse or refined, beautiful or ugly, well-born or poorly-born according to the consequences of their actions ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: With clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, they see sentient beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, in a good place or a bad place. They understand how sentient beings pass on according to their deeds.

segments.pali: Āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the exhaustion of the outflows, he dwells having seen personally and attained in this present life with direct knowledge, by himself the freedoms of mind and discernment that are free of outflow.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life. And they live having realized it with their own insight due to the ending of defilements.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the six things that are to be seen for oneself.

segments.pali: Iti ime saṭṭhi dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These sixty things which have been rightly and fully enlightened to thus by the Such-Attained One are true, real, just so, not false, and not otherwise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: So these sixty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: 7. Sevens

english.author: sujato
english.text: 7. Groups of Seven

segments.pali: Satta dhammā bahukārā …pe… satta dhammā sacchikātabbā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are seven things that are of great help; seven things that are to be cultivated; seven things that are to be understood accurately; seven things that are to be abandoned; seven things that lead to backsliding; seven things that lead to accomplishment; seven things that are hard to penetrate; seven things that are to be encouraged; seven things that are to be understood fully; seven things that are to be seen for oneself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven things are helpful, etc.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are of great help?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things are helpful?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven noble assets—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven riches of the noble ones:

segments.pali: saddhādhanaṁ, sīladhanaṁ, hiridhanaṁ, ottappadhanaṁ, sutadhanaṁ, cāgadhanaṁ, paññādhanaṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The asset of faith; the asset of virtue; the asset of conscience; the asset of imperative propriety; the asset of study; the asset of giving; the asset of discernment.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the riches of faith, ethics, conscience, prudence, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are of great help.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are to be cultivated?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things should be developed?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven factors of enlightenment—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven awakening factors:

segments.pali: satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Mindfulness; exploration of phenomena; energy; rapture; tranquility; collectedness; stoic composure.

english.author: sujato
english.text: mindfulness, investigation of principles, energy, rapture, tranquility, immersion, and equanimity.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are to be cultivated.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are to be understood accurately?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things should be completely understood?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven abidings of consciousness—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven planes of consciousness.

segments.pali: santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, namely: humans, some angels, and some beings of fallen birth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of diverse bodies and unified perception, namely: angels of the gods' retinue reborn there from the first [jhāna].

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the second abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of unified bodies and unified perception, namely: the radiant angels.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of streaming radiance.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the third abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of unified bodies and unified perception, namely: the lustrous angels.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fourth abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā …pe… ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, with the transcendence of perceptions of form altogether ... attain to the sphere of infinite space, percipient ‘Space is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fifth abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, transcending the sphere of infinite space altogether, attain to the sphere of infinite consciousness, percipient ‘Consciousness is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the sixth abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth plane of consciousness.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness altogether, attain to the sphere of no possessions, percipient ‘There is nothing’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the seventh abiding of consciousness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh plane of consciousness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are to be understood accurately.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are to be abandoned?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things should be given up?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven subconscious proclivities—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven underlying tendencies:

segments.pali: kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo, vicikicchānusayo, mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Sensual passion; aversion; views; apprehension; conceit; passion for existence; ignorance.

english.author: sujato
english.text: sensual desire, aversion, views, doubt, conceit, desire for continued existence, and ignorance.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are to be abandoned.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that lead to backsliding?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things make things worse?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven unrighteousnesses—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven bad qualities:

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu assaddho hoti, ahiriko hoti, anottappī hoti, appassuto hoti, kusīto hoti, muṭṭhassati hoti, duppañño hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk lacks faith, lacks conscience, lacks imperative propriety, has studied little, is lazy, inattentive to mindfulness, and is undiscerning.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a mendicant is faithless, shameless, imprudent, unlearned, lazy, unmindful, and witless.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that lead to backsliding.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that lead to accomplishment?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things lead to distinction?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven righteousnesses—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven good qualities:

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu saddho hoti, hirimā hoti, ottappī hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, upaṭṭhitassati hoti, paññavā hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has faith, conscience, imperative propriety, has studied much; is of resolute energy, has ready and present mindfulness, and is discerning.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a mendicant is faithful, conscientious, prudent, learned, energetic, mindful, and wise.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that lead to accomplishment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are hard to penetrate?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things are hard to comprehend?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven qualities of people of integrity—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven aspects of the teachings of the true persons:

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu dhammaññū ca hoti atthaññū ca attaññū ca mattaññū ca kālaññū ca parisaññū ca puggalaññū ca.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here a monk has Dhammic intelligence, qualitative intelligence, intrapersonal intelligence, quantitative intelligence, temporal intelligence, social intelligence, and interpersonal intelligence.

english.author: sujato
english.text: a mendicant knows the teachings, knows the meaning, knows themselves, knows moderation, knows the right time, knows assemblies, and knows individuals.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are hard to penetrate.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are to be encouraged?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things should be produced?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven perceptions—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven perceptions:

segments.pali: aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, asubhasaññā, ādīnavasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The perception of impermanence; the perception of not-self; the perception of the unbeautiful; the perception of danger; the perception of abandoning; the perception of dispassion; the perception of ending.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of ugliness, the perception of drawbacks, the perception of giving up, the perception of fading away, and the perception of cessation.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are to be encouraged.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are to be understood fully?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things should be directly known?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven bases for spiritual seniority—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven qualifications for graduation.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu sikkhāsamādāne tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca sikkhāsamādāne avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has an intense desire for undertaking the training, and, in the future, that love for undertaking the training is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has a keen enthusiasm to undertake the training …

segments.pali: Dhammanisantiyā tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca dhammanisantiyā avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He has an intense desire for internalizing the Dhamma, and, in the future, that love for internalizing the Dhamma is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to examine the teachings …

segments.pali: Icchāvinaye tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca icchāvinaye avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He has an intense desire for dispelling worldly wants, and, in the future, that love for dispelling worldly wants is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to get rid of desires …

segments.pali: Paṭisallāne tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca paṭisallāne avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He has an intense desire for retreat, and, in the future, that love for retreat is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: for retreat …

segments.pali: Vīriyārambhe tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca vīriyārambhe avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He has an intense desire for putting forth energy, and, in the future, that love for putting forth energy is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to rouse up energy …

segments.pali: Satinepakke tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca satinepakke avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He has an intense desire for maturity of mindfulness, and, in the future, that love for maturity of mindfulness is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: for mindfulness and alertness …

segments.pali: Diṭṭhipaṭivedhe tibbacchando hoti, āyatiñca diṭṭhipaṭivedhe avigatapemo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He has an intense desire for penetration of view, and, in the future, that love for penetration of view is not lost.

english.author: sujato
english.text: to penetrate theoretically. And they don’t lose these desires in the future.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are to be understood fully.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the seven things that are to be seen for oneself?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What seven things should be realized?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The seven powers of one who has exhausted the outflows—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Seven powers of one who has ended the defilements.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk who has exhausted the outflows accurately and truly sees with right discernment that all conditioned phenomena are impermanent.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom all conditions as truly impermanent.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti, idampi khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti: ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim: ‘My defilements have ended.’

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk who has exhausted the outflows accurately and truly sees with right discernment that sensual pleasures are like a pit of burning coals.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has clearly seen with right wisdom that sensual pleasures are truly like a pit of glowing coals. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṁ cittaṁ hoti vivekapoṇaṁ vivekapabbhāraṁ vivekaṭṭhaṁ nekkhammābhirataṁ byantībhūtaṁ sabbaso āsavaṭṭhāniyehi dhammehi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, the mind of a monk who has exhausted the outflows leans toward disentanglement, slopes toward disentanglement, inclines to disentanglement, and has disentanglement as its aim. It delights in renunciation and has altogether done away with any bases for the outflows.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, the mind of a mendicant with defilements ended slants, slopes, and inclines to seclusion. They’re withdrawn, loving renunciation, and have totally eliminated defiling influences. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk who has exhausted the outflows has cultivated, thoroughly cultivated, the four cornerstones of mindfulness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the four kinds of mindfulness meditation. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni honti subhāvitāni.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk who has exhausted the outflows has cultivated, thoroughly cultivated, the five faculties.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the five faculties. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk who has exhausted the outflows has cultivated, thoroughly cultivated, the seven factors of enlightenment.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the seven awakening factors. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk who has exhausted the outflows has cultivated, thoroughly cultivated, the noble eightfold path.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant with defilements ended has well developed the noble eightfold path. …

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito, idampi khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṁ hoti, yaṁ balaṁ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayaṁ paṭijānāti:

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For a monk who has exhausted the outflows, this is a power with regards to which he knows

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is a power that a mendicant who has ended the defilements relies on to claim:

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘For me, the outflows are exhausted’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘My defilements have ended.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the seven things that are to be seen for oneself.

segments.pali: Itime sattati dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These seventy things which have been rightly and fully enlightened to thus by the Such-Attained One are true, real, just so, not false, and not otherwise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: So these seventy things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The first recitation section is complete.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The first recitation section is complete.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: 8. Eights

english.author: sujato
english.text: 8. Groups of Eight

segments.pali: Aṭṭha dhammā bahukārā …pe… aṭṭha dhammā sacchikātabbā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are eight things that are of great help; eight things that are to be cultivated; eight things that are to be understood accurately; eight things that are to be abandoned; eight things that lead to backsliding; eight things that lead to accomplishment; eight things that are hard to penetrate; eight things that are to be encouraged; eight things that are to be understood fully; eight things that are to be seen for oneself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight things are helpful, etc.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are of great help?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things are helpful?

segments.pali: Aṭṭha hetū aṭṭha paccayā ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattanti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are eight causes, eight supports that lead to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are eight causes and reasons that lead to acquiring the wisdom fundamental to the spiritual life, and to its increase, growth, development, and fulfillment once it has been acquired.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What eight?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satthāraṁ upanissāya viharati aññataraṁ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṁ sabrahmacāriṁ, yatthassa tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti pemañca gāravo ca.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk dwells in dependence on a teacher or on a certain one of his fellows in the holy life in the place of a teacher and he is consistently grounded with an intense sense of conscience, imperative propriety, love, and respect for them.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant lives relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role. And they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for them, with warmth and respect.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ paṭhamo hetu paṭhamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first cause, the first support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first cause.

segments.pali: Taṁ kho pana satthāraṁ upanissāya viharati aññataraṁ vā garuṭṭhāniyaṁ sabrahmacāriṁ, yatthassa tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti pemañca gāravo ca. Te kālena kālaṁ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati paripañhati:

english.author: kovilo
english.text: While dwelling in dependence on a teacher or on a certain one of his fellows in the holy life in the place of a teacher and while consistently grounded with an intense sense of conscience, imperative propriety, love, and respect for them, he further, from time to time, approaches them and inquires and asks questions:

english.author: sujato
english.text: When a mendicant lives relying on the Teacher or a spiritual companion in a teacher’s role—with a keen sense of conscience and prudence for them, with warmth and respect—from time to time they go and ask them questions:

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Venerable, why it this as it is?

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘Why, sir, does it say this?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What is the meaning of this?’

english.author: sujato
english.text: What does that mean?’

segments.pali: Tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodenti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That Venerable clarifies what was unclear, elucidates what was obscure, and through various means eliminates his doubt regarding dubious things.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Those venerables clarify what is unclear, reveal what is obscure, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ dutiyo hetu dutiyo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya, vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the second cause, the second support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second cause.

segments.pali: Taṁ kho pana dhammaṁ sutvā dvayena vūpakāsena sampādeti—kāyavūpakāsena ca cittavūpakāsena ca.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, having heard the teaching, he strives by twofold seclusion—physical seclusion and mental seclusion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: After hearing that teaching they perfect withdrawal of both body and mind.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ tatiyo hetu tatiyo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the third cause, the third support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third cause.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And further, the monk is virtuous. He dwells restrained by the restraint of the monk's rules, is skilled in his behavior, and chooses his environment wisely. He sees danger in the slightest faults and, having taken them on, he trains himself according to the training precepts.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ catuttho hetu catuttho paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fourth cause, the fourth support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth cause.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And further, he has studied much and remembered what he has heard of those teachings—beautiful in the beginning, middle, and end—which declare the utterly complete and pure holy life with its essentials and features. He has studied, memorized, verbally recited, intellectually examined, and, with vision, has thoroughly realized the point of these sorts of teachings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is very learned, remembering and keeping what they’ve learned. These teachings are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, describing a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure. They are very learned in such teachings, remembering them, rehearsing them, mentally scrutinizing them, and penetrating them theoretically.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ pañcamo hetu pañcamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fifth cause, the fifth support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth cause.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And further, he dwells with resolute energy for the purpose of abandoning unwholesome mental states and for arousing wholesome mental states. He is steadfast, firm in his exertion, and is not remiss in his responsibilities regarding wholesome mental states.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ chaṭṭho hetu chaṭṭho paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the sixth cause, the sixth support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth cause.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato. Cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And further, he is mindful, endowed with exceptional memory and attentiveness. He is one who remembers and recollects even what was done and said long ago.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

segments.pali: Ayaṁ sattamo hetu sattamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the seventh cause, the seventh support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh cause.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu, udayabbayānupassī viharati:

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And further, he dwells observing the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of attachment:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

segments.pali: ‘iti rūpaṁ iti rūpassa samudayo iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Such is form. Such is form's origin. Such is form's cessation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

segments.pali: iti vedanā iti vedanāya samudayo iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Such is feeling. Such is feeling's origin. Such is feeling's cessation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the ending of feeling.

segments.pali: iti saññā iti saññāya samudayo iti saññāya atthaṅgamo;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Such is perception. Such is perception's origin. Such is perception's cessation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the ending of perception.

segments.pali: iti saṅkhārā iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Such are volitional actions. Such are volitional actions' origin. Such are volitional actions' cessation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the ending of choices.

segments.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ iti viññāṇassa samudayo iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Such is consciousness. Such is consciousness's origin. Such is consciousness's cessation.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness.’

segments.pali: Ayaṁ aṭṭhamo hetu aṭṭhamo paccayo ādibrahmacariyikāya paññāya appaṭiladdhāya paṭilābhāya, paṭiladdhāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā saṁvattati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the eighth cause, the eighth support that leads to acquiring the unacquired discernment that is foundational to one living the holy life, and to furthering, increasing, cultivating, and fulfilling that which has been acquired.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth cause.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are of great help.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are to be cultivated?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things should be developed?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The noble eightfold path, namely—

english.author: sujato
english.text: The noble eightfold path, that is:

segments.pali: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Right View; Right Thought; Right Speech; Right Action; Right Livelihood; Right Effort; Right Mindfulness; Right Collectedness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are to be cultivated.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are to be understood accurately?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things should be completely understood?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The eight worldly phenomena—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight worldly conditions:

segments.pali: lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṁsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañca.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Gain and loss; popularity and disgrace; praise and blame; pleasure and pain.

english.author: sujato
english.text: gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are to be understood accurately.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are to be abandoned?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things should be given up?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The eight wrongnesses—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight wrong ways:

segments.pali: micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Wrong view; wrong thought; wrong speech; wrong action; wrong livelihood; wrong effort; wrong mindfulness; wrong collectedness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong immersion.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are to be abandoned.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that lead to backsliding?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things make things worse?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The eight bases of laziness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight grounds for laziness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, there is work to be done by a monk,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Firstly, a mendicant has some work to do.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: and he thinks:

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘kammaṁ kho me kātabbaṁ bhavissati, kammaṁ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilamissati, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘I have work to do. When doing the work, my body will get tired. Why don't I take a nap.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I have some work to do. But while doing it my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

segments.pali: So nipajjati, na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: So he takes a nap and doesn't kindle energy for attaining the unattained, acquiring the unacquired, or seeing for himself that which he has not seen for himself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first bases of laziness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā kammaṁ kataṁ hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Or alternatively, a monk has completed some work,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has done some work.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: and he thinks:

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho kammaṁ akāsiṁ, kammaṁ kho pana me karontassa kāyo kilanto, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘I have completed some work. When doing the work, my body got tired. Why don't I take a nap.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve done some work. But while working my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: So he takes a nap and doesn't kindle energy for attaining the unattained, acquiring the unacquired, or seeing for himself that which he has not seen for himself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the second bases of laziness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gantabbo hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Or alternatively, a monk has a trip to make,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has to go on a journey.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: and he thinks:

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘maggo kho me gantabbo bhavissati, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilamissati, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘I have a trip to take. When taking the trip, my body will get tired. Why don't I take a nap.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I have to go on a journey. But while walking my body will get tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: So he takes a nap and doesn't kindle energy for attaining the unattained, acquiring the unacquired, or seeing for himself that which he has not seen for himself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They lie down, and don’t rouse energy…

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the third bases of laziness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third ground for laziness.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhunā maggo gato hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Or alternatively, a monk has completed a trip,

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has gone on a journey.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: and he thinks:

english.author: sujato
english.text: They think:

segments.pali: ‘ahaṁ kho maggaṁ agamāsiṁ, maggaṁ kho pana me gacchantassa kāyo kilanto, handāhaṁ nipajjāmī’ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘I have completed a trip. When taking the trip, my body got tired. Why don't I take a nap.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘I’ve gone on a journey. But while walking my body got tired. I’d better have a lie down.’

english.author: kovilo

segments.pali: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ, natthi hutaṁ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalaṁ vipāko, natthi ayaṁ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.

english.text: ‘What is offered is null. What is sacrificed is null. What is bestowed is null. The fruit and result of good and bad action are null. This world does not exist. A further world does not exist. There is no mother. There is no father. There are no spontaneously reborn beings. There are no right living, right practicing recluses or brahmans in the world who teach about this world and a further world having seen them personally with direct knowledge.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’
