segments.pali: ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti duppañño jaḷo eḷamūgo, nappaṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This person is reborn amongst the people of the central country, but he is undiscerning, slow-witted, deaf, mute, and is unable to understand the distinction between what is well-said and what is poorly-said.

english.author: sujato
english.text: And an individual is reborn in a central country. But they’re witless, dull, idiotic, and unable to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the seventh inopportune, inconvenient occasion for living the holy life.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Or alternatively, a Such-Attained One, a Worthy One, a Fully Enlightened Buddha has not arisen in the world. And so does not teach the Dhamma that leads to peace, that leads to Nibbāna, that leads to full enlightenment, that is declared by those Well Gone.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, no Realized One has arisen in the world,

segments.pali: ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti paññavā ajaḷo aneḷamūgo, paṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And this person is reborn amongst the people of the central country, is discerning, is quick-witted, can hear and speak, and is able to understand the distinction between what is well-said and what is poorly-said.

english.author: sujato
english.text: so there is no teaching of the Dhamma leading to peace, extinguishment, awakening, as proclaimed by the Holy One. But an individual is reborn in a central country. And they’re wise, bright, clever, and able to distinguish what is well said from what is poorly said.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the eighth inopportune, inconvenient occasion for living the holy life.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth lost opportunity for spiritual practice.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are hard to penetrate.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are to be encouraged?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things should be produced?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The eight thoughts of a great man—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight thoughts of a great man.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for one of few longings, not for one of many longings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘This teaching is for those of few wishes, not those of many wishes.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for the contented, not for the discontented.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s for the contented, not those who lack contentment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for the disentangled, not for one who loves company.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s for the secluded, not those who enjoy company.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for one of resolute energy, not for the lazy.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s for the energetic, not the lazy.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for one whose mindfulness is established, not for the absent minded.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s for the mindful, not the unmindful.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for the settled, not for the unsettled.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s for those with immersion, not those without immersion.

segments.pali: Paññavato ayaṁ dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo duppaññassa.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for the discerning, not for the undiscerning.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s for the wise, not the witless.

segments.pali: Nippapañcassāyaṁ dhammo, nāyaṁ dhammo papañcārāmassāti ime aṭṭha dhammā uppādetabbā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This teaching is for the uncomplicated, not for one who loves complication. These are the eight things that are to be encouraged.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This teaching is for those who don’t enjoy proliferating, not for those who enjoy proliferating.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are to be understood fully?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things should be directly known?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The eight spheres of mastery—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight dimensions of mastery.

segments.pali: ajjhattaṁ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Someone percipient of form internally sees both beautiful and ugly external forms as insignificant. And he has this perception—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of form as singular internally, one sees both beautiful and ugly external forms as boundless. And he has this perception—XXXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the second sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Someone percipient of the formless internally sees both beautiful and ugly external forms as insignificant. And he has this perception—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limited, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the third sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti—

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of the formless as singular internally, one sees both beautiful and ugly external forms as boundless. And he has this perception—XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally, limitless, both pretty and ugly. Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: ‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fourth sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of the formless as singular internally, one sees external forms as blue, blue colored, blue in characteristics, blue in shine.XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṁ nīlaṁ nīlavaṇṇaṁ nīlanidassanaṁ nīlanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ nīlaṁ nīlavaṇṇaṁ nīlanidassanaṁ nīlanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Just as a flax flower is blue, blue colored, blue in characteristics, blue in shine; or just as fabric from Varanasi that is polished on both sides is blue, blue colored, blue in characteristics, blue in shine—

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like a flax flower that’s blue, with blue color and blue appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, blue, with blue color and blue appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: in the same way, one is percipient of the formless as singular internally, and sees external forms as blue, blue colored, blue in characteristics, blue in shine. And he has this perception—‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fifth sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of the formless as singular internally, one sees external forms as yellow, yellow colored, yellow in characteristics, yellow in shine.XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṁ pītaṁ pītavaṇṇaṁ pītanidassanaṁ pītanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ pītaṁ pītavaṇṇaṁ pītanidassanaṁ pītanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Just as a kaṇikāra flower is yellow, yellow colored, yellow in characteristics, yellow in shine; or just as fabric from Varanasi that is polished on both sides is yellow, yellow colored, yellow in characteristics, yellow in shine—

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like a champak flower that’s yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, yellow, with yellow color and yellow appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: in the same way, one is percipient of the formless as singular internally, and sees external forms as yellow, yellow colored, yellow in characteristics, yellow in shine. And he has this perception—‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the sixth sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of the formless as singular internally, one sees external forms as red, red colored, red in characteristics, red in shine.XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are red, with red color and red appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṁ lohitakaṁ lohitakavaṇṇaṁ lohitakanidassanaṁ lohitakanibhāsaṁ, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ lohitakaṁ lohitakavaṇṇaṁ lohitakanidassanaṁ lohitakanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Just as a Scarlet Mallow flower is red, red colored, red in characteristics, red in shine; or just as fabric from Varanasi that is polished on both sides is red, red colored, red in characteristics, red in shine—

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like a scarlet mallow flower that’s red, with red color and red appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, red, with red color and red appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: in the same way, one is percipient of the formless as singular internally, and sees external forms as red, red colored, red in characteristics, red in shine. And he has this perception—‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the seventh sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh dimension of mastery.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of the formless as singular internally, one sees external forms as white, white colored, white in characteristics, white in shine.XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving form internally, someone sees forms externally that are white, with white color and white appearance.

segments.pali: Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā, seyyathā vā pana taṁ vatthaṁ bārāṇaseyyakaṁ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṁ odātaṁ odātavaṇṇaṁ odātanidassanaṁ odātanibhāsaṁ;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Just as the morning star is white, white colored, white in characteristics, white in shine; or just as fabric from Varanasi that is polished on both sides is white, white colored, white in characteristics, white in shine—

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re like the morning star that’s white, with white color and white appearance. Or a cloth from Varanasi that’s smoothed on both sides, white, with white color and white appearance.

segments.pali: evameva ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṁsaññī hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: in the same way, one is percipient of the formless as singular internally, and sees external forms as white, white colored, white in characteristics, white in shine. And he has this perception—‘Having mastered those, I know and see.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Mastering them, they perceive: ‘I know and see.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the eigth sphere of mastery.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth dimension of mastery.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are to be understood fully.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the eight things that are to be seen for oneself?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What eight things should be realized?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The eight liberations—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Eight liberations.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One sees forms as having form.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Having physical form, they see forms.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first liberation.

segments.pali: Ajjhattaṁ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Percipient of the formless as singular internally, one sees external forms. (XXXHOW DO WE TAKE "eko" HERE?XXX)XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: Not perceiving physical form internally, someone see forms externally.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the second liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second liberation.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is intent only on ‘beautiful.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: They’re focused only on beauty.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the third liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of perceptions of form altogether, and the cessation of perceptions of aversion, not attending to perceptions of diversity, one attains and dwells in the sphere of infinite space, percipient ‘Space is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fourth liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of infinite space altogether, one attains and dwells in the sphere of infinite consciousness, percipient ‘Consciousness is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fifth liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of infinite consciousness altogether, one attains and dwells in the sphere of no possessions, percipient ‘There is nothing’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the sixth liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of no possessions altogether, one attains and dwells in the sphere of neither perception nor non perception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the seventh liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh liberation.

segments.pali: Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of neither perception nor non perception altogether, one attains and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the eight liberation.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth liberation.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the eight things that are to be seen for oneself.

segments.pali: Iti ime asīti dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These eighty things which have been rightly and fully enlightened to thus by the Such-Attained One are true, real, just so, not false, and not otherwise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: So these eighty things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: 9. Nines

english.author: sujato
english.text: 9. Groups of Nine

segments.pali: Nava dhammā bahukārā …pe… nava dhammā sacchikātabbā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are nine things that are of great help; nine things that are to be cultivated; nine things that are to be understood accurately; nine things that are to be abandoned; nine things that lead to backsliding; nine things that lead to accomplishment; nine things that are hard to penetrate; nine things that are to be encouraged; nine things that are to be understood fully; nine things that are to be seen for oneself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine things are helpful, etc.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are of great help?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things are helpful?

segments.pali: Nava yonisomanasikāramūlakā dhammā, yonisomanasikaroto pāmojjaṁ jāyati, pamuditassa pīti jāyati, pītimanassa kāyo passambhati, passaddhakāyo sukhaṁ vedeti, sukhino cittaṁ samādhiyati, samāhite citte yathābhūtaṁ jānāti passati, yathābhūtaṁ jānaṁ passaṁ nibbindati, nibbindaṁ virajjati, virāgā vimuccati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine mental states rooted in mature assessment. For one assessing maturely, gladness arises. For one who is glad, joy arises. For one of joyful mind, the body relaxes. One who's body is relaxed experiences ease. The mind of one experiencing ease becomes collected. When the mind is collected, one knows and sees accurately. Knowing and seeing accurately, one becomes disillusioned. Becoming disillusioned, one becomes dispassionate. From dispassion, one is released.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine things rooted in rational application of mind. When you apply the mind rationally, joy springs up. When you’re joyful, rapture springs up. When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil. When the body is tranquil, you feel bliss. And when you’re blissful, the mind becomes immersed. When your mind is immersed, you truly know and see. When you truly know and see, you grow disillusioned. Being disillusioned, desire fades away. When desire fades away you’re freed.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are of great help.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are to be cultivated?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things should be developed?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine factors of purity connected with exertion—(XXXPERHAPS LITERALLY "nine factors connected with exertion for the purpose of purity" (DATIVE OF AIM/PURPOSE)XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine factors of trying to be pure.

segments.pali: sīlavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, cittavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, diṭṭhivisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, kaṅkhāvitaraṇavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, maggāmaggañāṇadassanavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, paṭipadāñāṇadassanavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, ñāṇadassanavisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, paññāvisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ, vimuttivisuddhi pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Purity through virtue; purity through mind; purity through view; purity through overcoming doubt; purity through knowing and seeing what is the path and what isn't; purity through knowing and seeing the practice; purity through knowledge and vision; purity through discernment; purity through freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: The factors of trying to be pure in ethics, mind, view, overcoming doubt, knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path, knowledge and vision of the practice, knowledge and vision, wisdom, and freedom.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are to be cultivated.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are to be understood accurately?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things should be completely understood?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine abodes of beings—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine abodes of sentient beings.

segments.pali: santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of diverse bodies and diverse perceptions, namely: humans, some angels, and some beings of fallen birth.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and diverse in perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the first abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the first abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of diverse bodies and unified perception, namely: angels of the gods' retinue reborn there from the first [jhāna].

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are diverse in body and unified in perception, such as the gods reborn in the Divinity’s host through the first absorption.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the second abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the second abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of unified bodies and unified perception, namely: the radiant angels.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and diverse in perception, such as the gods of streaming radiance.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the third abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the third abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings of unified bodies and unified perception, namely: the lustrous angels.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are unified in body and unified in perception, such as the gods of universal beauty.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fourth abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fourth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā asaññino appaṭisaṁvedino, seyyathāpi devā asaññasattā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who have no perception and feel nothing, namely: the no perception angels.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that are non-percipient and do not experience anything, such as the gods who are non-percipient beings.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the fifth abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the fifth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, with the transcendence of perceptions of form altogether, and the cessation of perceptions of aversion, not attending to perceptions of diversity, attain to the sphere of infinite space, percipient ‘Space is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond perceptions of form. With the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite space.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the sixth abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the sixth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, transcending the sphere of infinite space altogether, attain to the sphere of infinite consciousness, percipient ‘Consciousness is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite space. Aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they have been reborn in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the seventh abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the seventh abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness altogether, attain to the sphere of no possessions, percipient ‘There is nothing’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness. Aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they have been reborn in the dimension of nothingness.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the eigth abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the eighth abode of sentient beings.

segments.pali: Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are beings who, transcending the sphere of no possessions altogether, attain to the sphere of neither perception nor non perception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: There are sentient beings that have gone totally beyond the dimension of nothingness. They have been reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: This is the ninth abode of beings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is the ninth abode of sentient beings.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are to be understood accurately.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are to be abandoned?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things should be given up?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine things rooted in craving—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine things rooted in craving.

segments.pali: taṇhaṁ paṭicca pariyesanā, pariyesanaṁ paṭicca lābho, lābhaṁ paṭicca vinicchayo, vinicchayaṁ paṭicca chandarāgo, chandarāgaṁ paṭicca ajjhosānaṁ, ajjhosānaṁ paṭicca pariggaho, pariggahaṁ paṭicca macchariyaṁ, macchariyaṁ paṭicca ārakkho, ārakkhādhikaraṇaṁ daṇḍādānasatthādānakalahaviggahavivādatuvaṁtuvaṁpesuññamusāvādā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Because of craving, there is searching. Because of searching, there is gain. Because of gain, there is speculation. Because of speculation, there is passionate desire. Because of passionate desire, there is acquisitiveness. Because of acquisitiveness, there is possessiveness. Because of possessiveness, there is stinginess. Because of stinginess, there is mercenariness. Because of mercenariness, manifold vile, unwholesome things manifest: the taking up of clubs and weapons; quarreling, disputing, contention, and strife; and backbiting and lying.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Craving gives rise to searching. Searching gives rise to gaining material things. Gaining material things gives rise to evaluation. Evaluation gives rise to desire and lust. Desire and lust gives rise to attachment. Attachment gives rise to ownership. Ownership gives rise to stinginess. Stinginess gives rise to safeguarding. Owing to safeguarding, many bad, unskillful things come to be: taking up the rod and the sword, quarrels, arguments, disputes, accusations, backbiting, and lies.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are to be abandoned.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that lead to backsliding?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things make things worse?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine bases of resentment:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine grounds for resentment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They pursued my disadvantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me,’ you harbor resentment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They are pursuing my disadvantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They will pursue my disadvantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong to me’ …

segments.pali: ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṁ acarī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati …pe…

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They pursued my friend's disadvantage, my dear one's disadvantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They did wrong by someone I love’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They are pursuing my friend's disadvantage, my dear one's disadvantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are doing wrong by someone I love’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They will pursue my friend's disadvantage, my dear one's disadvantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong by someone I love’ …

segments.pali: ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṁ acarī’ti āghātaṁ bandhati …pe…

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They pursued my enemy's advantage, my opponent's advantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They helped someone I dislike’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They are pursuing my enemy's advantage, my opponent's advantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are helping someone I dislike’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is bound in resentment thinking ‘They will pursue my enemy's advantage, my opponent's advantage.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike,’ you harbor resentment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that lead to backsliding.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that lead to accomplishment?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things lead to distinction?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine ways of resolving resentment:

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine ways to get rid of resentment.

segments.pali: ‘anatthaṁ me acari, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One resolves resentment thinking ‘They pursued my disadvantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They did wrong to me, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

segments.pali: ‘anatthaṁ me carati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One resolves resentment thinking ‘They are pursuing my disadvantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They are doing wrong to me …’ …

segments.pali: ‘anatthaṁ me carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One resolves resentment thinking ‘They will pursue my disadvantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong to me …’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One resolves resentment thinking ‘They pursued my friend's disadvantage, my dear one's disadvantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They did wrong by someone I love …’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One resolves resentment thinking ‘They are pursuing my friend's disadvantage, my dear one's disadvantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are doing wrong by someone I love …’ …

segments.pali: anatthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti;

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One resolves resentment thinking ‘They will pursue my friend's disadvantage, my dear one's disadvantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They will do wrong by someone I love …’ …

english.author: kovilo
