english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They helped someone I dislike …’ …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is resolves resentment thinking ‘They are pursuing my enemy's advantage, my opponent's advantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: ‘They are helping someone I dislike …’ …

segments.pali: atthaṁ carissati, taṁ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṁ paṭivineti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One is resolves resentment thinking ‘They will pursue my enemy's advantage, my opponent's advantage. But how is resentment beneficial here?’ (XXXOR "But what is gained here for him?"XXX)

english.author: sujato
english.text: Thinking: ‘They will help someone I dislike, but what can I possibly do?’ you get rid of resentment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that lead to accomplishment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are hard to penetrate?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things are hard to comprehend?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine variousnesses—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine kinds of diversity.

segments.pali: dhātunānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati phassanānattaṁ, phassanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati vedanānānattaṁ, vedanānānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saññānānattaṁ, saññānānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati saṅkappanānattaṁ, saṅkappanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati chandanānattaṁ, chandanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati pariḷāhanānattaṁ, pariḷāhanānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati pariyesanānānattaṁ, pariyesanānānattaṁ paṭicca uppajjati lābhanānattaṁ (…).

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Based on the variety of elements, the variety of contacts arise. Based on the variety of contacts, the variety of feelings arise. Based on the variety of feelings, the variety of perceptions arise. Based on the variety of perceptions, the variety of thoughts arise. Based on the variety of thoughts, the variety of desires arise. Based on the variety of desires, the variety of passions arise. Based on the variety of passions, the variety of search arise. Based on the variety of search, the variety of acquisition arise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Diversity of elements gives rise to diversity of contacts. Diversity of contacts gives rise to diversity of feelings. Diversity of feelings gives rise to diversity of perceptions. Diversity of perceptions gives rise to diversity of thoughts. Diversity of thoughts gives rise to diversity of desires. Diversity of desires gives rise to diversity of passions. Diversity of passions gives rise to diversity of searches. Diversity of searches gives rise to diversity of gains.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are hard to penetrate.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are to be encouraged?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things should be produced?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine perceptions—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine perceptions:

segments.pali: asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text:
The perception of the unbeautiful; the perception of death; the perception of disinclination toward food; the perception of boredom toward the whole world; the perception of impermanence; the perception of suffering regarding that which is impermanent; the perception of not-self regarding that which is suffering;  
the perception of abandoning; the perception of dispassion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the perceptions of ugliness, death, repulsiveness in food, dissatisfaction with the whole world, impermanence, suffering in impermanence, not-self in suffering, giving up, and fading away.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are to be encouraged.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are to be understood fully?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things should be directly known?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine successive dwellings—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine progressive meditations.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, having disentangled himself from sensual pleasures and from unwholesome mental states, a monk attains and dwells in the rapture and pleasure born of disentanglement and connected with thought and reflection, that is, the first meditative immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption …

segments.pali: Vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the calming of thought and reflection ... he attains and dwells in the second meditative immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: second absorption …

segments.pali: Pītiyā ca virāgā …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And with the fading of rapture ... he attains and dwells in the third meditative immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: third absorption …

segments.pali: Sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And with the abandoning of pleasure ... he attains and dwells in the fourth meditative immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: fourth absorption.

segments.pali: Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā …pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of perceptions of form altogether ... he attains and dwells in the sphere of infinite space.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite space.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of infinite space altogether, he attains and dwells in the sphere of infinite consciousness, percipient ‘Consciousness is infinite’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, they enter and remain in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of infinite consciousness altogether, he attains and dwells in the sphere of no possessions, percipient ‘There is nothing’.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, they enter and remain in the dimension of nothingness.

segments.pali: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of no possessions altogether, he attains and dwells in the sphere of neither perception nor non perception.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, they enter and remain in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segments.pali: Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With the transcendence of the sphere of neither perception nor non perception altogether, he attains and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Going totally beyond the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, they enter and remain in the cessation of perception and feeling.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are to be understood fully.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the nine things that are to be seen for oneself?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What nine things should be realized?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The nine successive endings—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Nine progressive cessations.

segments.pali: paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa kāmasaññā niruddhā hoti,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the first meditative immersion, the perception of sensual pleasure has ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the first absorption, sensual perceptions have ceased.

segments.pali: dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā niruddhā honti,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the second meditative immersion, thought and reflection have ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the second absorption, the placing of the mind and keeping it connected have ceased.

segments.pali: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa pīti niruddhā hoti,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the third meditative immersion, rapture has ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the third absorption, rapture has ceased.

segments.pali: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ samāpannassa assāsapassāssā niruddhā honti,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the fourth meditative immersion, out-breaths and in-breaths have ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the fourth absorption, breathing has ceased.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the sphere of infinite space, the perception of form has ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite space, the perception of form has ceased.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the sphere of infinite consciousness, the perception of the sphere of infinite space has ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of infinite consciousness, the perception of the dimension of infinite space has ceased.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the sphere of no possessions, the perception of the sphere of infinite consciousness has ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of nothingness, the perception of the dimension of infinite consciousness has ceased.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the sphere of neither perception nor non perception, the perception of the sphere of no possessions has ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, the perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased.

segments.pali: saññāvedayitanirodhaṁ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca niruddhā honti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one who has reached the cessation of perception and feeling, the perceptions and feelings have ended.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For someone who has attained the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the nine things that are to be seen for oneself.

segments.pali: Iti ime navuti dhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These ninety things which have been rightly and fully enlightened to thus by the Such-Attained One are true, real, just so, not false, and not otherwise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: So these ninety things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: 10. Tens

english.author: sujato
english.text: 10. Groups of Ten

segments.pali: Dasa dhammā bahukārā …pe… dasa dhammā sacchikātabbā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: There are ten things that are of great help; ten things that are to be cultivated; ten things that are to be understood accurately; ten things that are to be abandoned; ten things that lead to backsliding; ten things that lead to accomplishment; ten things that are hard to penetrate; ten things that are to be encouraged; ten things that are to be understood fully; ten things that are to be seen for oneself.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten things are helpful, ten things should be developed, ten things should be completely understood, ten things should be given up, ten things make things worse, ten things lead to distinction, ten things are hard to comprehend, ten things should be produced, ten things should be directly known, ten things should be realized.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are of great help?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things are helpful?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten practices that provide protection—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten qualities that serve as protector.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk is virtuous. He dwells restrained by the restraint of the monk's rules, is skilled in his behavior, and chooses his environment wisely. He sees danger in the slightest faults and, having taken them on, he trains himself according to the training precepts.

english.author: sujato
english.text: First, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segments.pali: Yaṁpāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk is virtuous ... and trains himself according to the training precepts,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto …pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk has studied much and remembered what he has heard of those teachings—beautiful in the beginning, middle, and end—which declare the utterly complete and pure holy life with its essentials and features. He has studied, memorized, verbally recited, intellectually examined, and, with vision, has thoroughly realized the point of these sorts of teachings.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is learned.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk has studied much ...

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk has admirable friends, admirable companions, and admirable associates.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... has admirable associates,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk is easy to talk to and has qualities that make him congenial. He is patient and receives instruction well.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is easy to admonish, having qualities that make them easy to admonish. They’re patient, and take instruction respectfully.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... receives instruction well,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṁ uccāvacāni kiṅkaraṇīyāni tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrupāyāya vīmaṁsāya samannāgato, alaṁ kātuṁ, alaṁ saṁvidhātuṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk is skilled and energetic at doing whatever high and low tasks are to be done there for his fellows in the holy life. And he is discriminating regarding their various means, knowing what is appropriate to do, and what is appropriate to arrange to have done.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is deft and tireless in a diverse spectrum of duties for their spiritual companions, understanding how to go about things in order to complete and organize the work.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... appropriate to arrange to have done,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk has love for the teaching, is pleasing in conversation, and takes great joy in the higher teaching and higher discipline.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant loves the teachings and is a delight to converse with, being full of joy in the teaching and training.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... takes great joy in the higher teaching and higher discipline,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarehi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk is content with any robe, almsfood, lodging, support for the sick, or medicinal requisite whatsoever.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... whatsoever,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati …pe… kusalesu dhammesu.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk dwells with resolute energy for the purpose of abandoning unwholesome mental states and for arousing wholesome mental states. He is steadfast, firm in his exertion, and is not remiss in his responsibilities regarding wholesome mental states.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is energetic.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... wholesome mental states,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk is mindful, endowed with exceptional memory and attentiveness. He is one who remembers and recollects even what was done and said long ago.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is mindful. They have utmost mindfulness and alertness, and can remember and recall what was said and done long ago.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... said long ago,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

segments.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato, ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Further, a monk is discerning and endowed with the discernment that attends to arising and passing, that is noble, penetrative, and leads rightly to the destruction of suffering.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Furthermore, a mendicant is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: That a monk ... to the destruction of suffering,

english.author: kovilo
english.text: this, too, is a practice that provides protection.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This too is a quality that serves as protector.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are of great help.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are to be cultivated?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things should be developed?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten objects for meditative focus—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten universal dimensions of meditation.

segments.pali: pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṁ adho tiriyaṁ advayaṁ appamāṇaṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on earth—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Someone perceives the meditation on universal earth above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on water—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They perceive the meditation on universal water …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on fire—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal fire …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on wind—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal air …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on blue—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal blue …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on yellow—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal yellow …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on red—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal red …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on white—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal white …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on space—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the meditation on universal space …

segments.pali: viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṁ adho tiriyaṁ advayaṁ appamāṇaṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: One perceives the meditative focus on consciousness—above, below, across, non-dual, and boundless.

english.author: sujato
english.text: They perceive the meditation on universal consciousness above, below, across, undivided and limitless.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are to be cultivated.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are to be understood accurately?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things should be completely understood?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten spheres—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten sense fields:

segments.pali: cakkhāyatanaṁ, rūpāyatanaṁ, sotāyatanaṁ, saddāyatanaṁ, ghānāyatanaṁ, gandhāyatanaṁ, jivhāyatanaṁ, rasāyatanaṁ, kāyāyatanaṁ, phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṁ.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The sphere of the eyes; the sphere of forms; the sphere of the ears; the sphere of sounds; the sphere of the nose; the sphere of smells; the sphere of the tongue; the sphere of tastes; the sphere of the body; the sphere of touch.

english.author: sujato
english.text: eye and sights, ear and sounds, nose and smells, tongue and tastes, body and touches.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are to be understood accurately.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are to be abandoned?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things should be given up?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten wrongnesses—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten wrong ways:

segments.pali: micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṁ, micchāvimutti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Wrong view; wrong thought; wrong speech; wrong action; wrong livelihood; wrong effort; wrong mindfulness; wrong collectedness; wrong knowledge; wrong freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: wrong view, wrong purpose, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong immersion, wrong knowledge, and wrong freedom.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are to be abandoned.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that lead to backsliding?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things make things worse?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten paths of unwholesome action—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten ways of doing unskillful deeds:

segments.pali: pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṁ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Killing living beings; taking what hasn't been given; sexual misconduct; speaking falsely; malicious speech; harsh speech; frivolous chatter; greediness; ill will; wrong view.

english.author: sujato
english.text: killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; covetousness, ill will, and wrong view.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that lead to backsliding.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that lead to accomplishment?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things lead to distinction?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten paths of wholesome action—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten ways of doing skillful deeds:

segments.pali: pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Refraining from killing living beings; refraining from taking what hasn't been given; refraining from sexual misconduct; refraining from speaking falsely; refraining from malicious speech; refraining from harsh speech; refraining from frivolous chatter; non greediness; non ill will; right view.

english.author: sujato
english.text: refraining from killing living creatures, stealing, and sexual misconduct; avoiding speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical; contentment, good will, and right view.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that lead to accomplishment.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are hard to penetrate?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things are hard to comprehend?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten noble states—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten abodes of the noble ones.

segments.pali: idhāvuso, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti, chaḷaṅgasamannāgato, ekārakkho, caturāpasseno, paṇunnapaccekasacco, samavayasaṭṭhesano, anāvilasaṅkappo, passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro, suvimuttacitto, suvimuttapañño.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has abandoned five marks; he is endowed with six marks; he has a single guard; he has four supports; he has put away individual truth assertions; he has dispensed with the search for conclusion; he has pure thoughts; his bodily condition (breathing) is relaxed; his mind is thoroughly freed; his discernment is thoroughly freed.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant has given up five factors, possesses six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth, has totally given up searching, has unsullied intentions, has stilled the physical process, and is well freed in mind and well freed by wisdom.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how has a monk abandoned five marks?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant given up five factors?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has abandoned sensual desire, ill will, mental stagnation and sluggishness, distraction and worry, and apprehension.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant has given up sensual desire, ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk has abandoned five marks.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has given up five factors.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how is a monk endowed with six marks?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant possess six factors?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk, having seen a form with the eye, is not elated nor dejected, but abides stoically composed, mindful, and integrally aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: A mendicant, seeing a sight with their eyes, is neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having heard a sound with the ear ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Hearing a sound with their ears …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having smelled an odor with the nose ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Smelling an odor with their nose …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having tasted a flavor with the tongue ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Tasting a flavor with their tongue …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having felt a touch via the body ...

english.author: sujato
english.text: Encountering a touch with their body …

segments.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Having cognized a thought with the mind, he is not elated nor dejected, but abides stoically composed, mindful, and integrally aware.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad. They remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu chaḷaṅgasamannāgato hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk is endowed with six marks.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant possesses six factors.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how does a monk have a single guard?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant have a single guard?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu satārakkhena cetasā samannāgato hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk's mind is guarded by mindfulness.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant’s heart is guarded by mindfulness.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu ekārakkho hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk has a single guard.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has a single guard.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how does a monk have four supports?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant have four supports?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṁ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṁ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṁ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṁ vinodeti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk, having deliberated, uses some things, rejects some things, avoids some things, and dispels some things.

english.author: sujato
english.text: After appraisal, a mendicant uses some things, endures some things, avoids some things, and gets rid of some things.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu caturāpasseno hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk has four supports.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has four supports.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how has a monk put away individual truth assertions?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno yāni tāni puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ puthupaccekasaccāni, sabbāni tāni nunnāni honti paṇunnāni cattāni vantāni muttāni pahīnāni paṭinissaṭṭhāni.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has driven out, put away, given up, vomited out, put down, abandoned, and renounced all the various, individual truth assertions of various recluses and brahmans.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Different ascetics and brahmins have different idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth. A mendicant has cast out, cast aside, thrown out, discarded, let go of, given up, and relinquished all these.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu paṇunnapaccekasacco hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk has put away individual truth assertions?

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has cast aside idiosyncratic interpretations of the truth.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how has a monk dispensed with the search for conclusion?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant totally given up searching?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmesanā pahīnā hoti, bhavesanā pahīnā hoti, brahmacariyesanā paṭippassaddhā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has abandoned the search for sensual pleasure; he has abandoned the search for becoming; he has allayed the search for a holy life.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when they’ve given up searching for sensual pleasures, for continued existence, and for a spiritual path.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu samavayasaṭṭhesano hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk has dispensed with the search for conclusion?.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has totally given up searching.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how does a monk has pure thoughts (XXXHOW TO TRANSLATE THIS PLURAL "saṅkappā"?XXX)?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how does a mendicant have unsullied intentions?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno kāmasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, byāpādasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, vihiṁsāsaṅkappo pahīno hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk has abandoned the thought of sensual pleasure; he has abandoned the thought of ill will; he has abandoned the thought of harming.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when they’ve given up sensual, malicious, and cruel intentions.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu anāvilasaṅkappo hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk has pure thoughts.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has unsullied intentions.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how is a monk's bodily condition (breathing) relaxed (XXXSINCE A BAHUBBIHI SUGGESTS 'has', CAN I TRANSLATE THE NOMINATIVE REFERENT OF THAT BAHUBBIHI AS A GENITIVE - "monk's"?XXX)?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how has a mendicant stilled the physical process?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, just as with the previous disappearance of mental cheer and anguish, a monk attains and dwells in neither pleasure nor pain, the purity of stoic composure and mindfulness that is the fourth meditative immersion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk's bodily condition (breathing) is relaxed.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant has stilled the physical process.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how is a monk's mind thoroughly freed (XXX SAME QUESTION ABOUT TRANSLATING BAHUBBIHI AS "monk's"?XXX)?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how is a mendicant well freed in mind?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhuno rāgā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, dosā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, mohā cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk's mind is thoroughly freed from passion; his mind is thoroughly freed from anger; his mind is thoroughly freed from delusion.

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant’s mind is freed from greed, hate, and delusion.

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttacitto hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk's mind is thoroughly freed.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant is well freed in mind.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And how is a monk's discernment thoroughly freed (XXX SAME QUESTION ABOUT TRANSLATING BAHUBBIHI AS "monk's"?XXX)?

english.author: sujato
english.text: And how is a mendicant well freed by wisdom?

segments.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ‘rāgo me pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Here, a monk knows: ‘I have abandoned (XXXTRANSLATING GENATIVE "me" AS HAVE?XXX) passion, destroyed its root, unearthed it like a palm tree, and made it extinct so that it will never arise again in the future.’

english.author: sujato
english.text: It’s when a mendicant understands: ‘I’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He knows: ‘I have abandoned anger ...

english.author: kovilo
english.text: so that it will never arise again in the future.’

english.author: kovilo
english.text: He knows: ‘I have abandoned delusion ...

english.author: kovilo
english.text: so that it will never arise again in the future.’

segments.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu suvimuttapañño hoti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: It is in this way that a monk's discernment thoroughly freed.

english.author: sujato
english.text: That’s how a mendicant’s mind is well freed by wisdom.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are hard to penetrate.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are to be encouraged?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things should be produced?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten perceptions—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten perceptions:

segments.pali: asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The perception of the unbeautiful; the perception of death; the perception of disinclination toward food; the perception of boredom toward the whole world; the perception of impermanence; the perception of suffering regarding that which is impermanent; the perception of not-self regarding that which is suffering;  the perception of abandoning; the perception of dispassion; the perception of ending.

english.author: sujato
english.text: the perceptions of ugliness, death, repulsiveness in food, dissatisfaction with the whole world, impermanence, suffering in impermanence, not-self in suffering, giving up, fading away, and cessation.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are to be encouraged.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are to be understood fully?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things should be directly known?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten bases for degeneration—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten grounds for wearing away.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right View, wrong view has been worn away.

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right view, wrong view is worn away.

segments.pali: Ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And for him, the manifold, vile, unwholesome mental states that manifest supported by wrong view have been worn away. XXXXAnd from wrong view as a condition what many, vile,  ... those too are worn away for himXXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong view are worn away.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Thought, wrong thought is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right intention, wrong intention is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Speech, wrong soeech is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right speech, wrong speech is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Action, wrong action is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right action, wrong action is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Livelihood, wrong livelihood is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right livelihood, wrong livelihood is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Effort, wrong effort is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right effort, wrong effort is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Collectedness, wrong collectedness is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right immersion, wrong immersion is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Knowledge, wrong knowledge is degeneration ...XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right knowledge, wrong knowledge is worn away. …

english.author: kovilo
english.text: For one of Right Freedom, wrong freedom is degeneration.XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: For one of right freedom, wrong freedom is worn away.

segments.pali: Ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: And the manifold vile, unwholesome mental states that manifest supported by wrong freedom are his degeneration.XXX

english.author: sujato
english.text: And the many bad, unskillful qualities that arise because of wrong freedom are worn away.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are to be understood fully.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: What are the ten things that are to be seen for oneself?

english.author: sujato
english.text: What ten things should be realized?

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The ten mental states of the graduate—

english.author: sujato
english.text: Ten qualities of an adept:

segments.pali: asekkhā sammādiṭṭhi, asekkho sammāsaṅkappo, asekkhā sammāvācā, asekkho sammākammanto, asekkho sammāājīvo, asekkho sammāvāyāmo, asekkhā sammāsati, asekkho sammāsamādhi, asekkhaṁ sammāñāṇaṁ, asekkhā sammāvimutti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Graduate Right View; graduate Right Thought; graduate Right Speech; graduate Right Action; graduate Right Livelihood; graduate Right Effort; graduate Right Mindfulness; graduate Right Collectedness; graduate Right Knowledge; graduate Right Freedom.

english.author: sujato
english.text: an adept’s right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These are the ten things that are to be seen for oneself.

segments.pali: Iti ime satadhammā bhūtā tacchā tathā avitathā anaññathā sammā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā”ti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: These hundred things which have been rightly and fully enlightened to thus by the Such-Attained One are true, real, just so, not false, and not otherwise.

english.author: sujato
english.text: So these hundred things that are true, real, and accurate, not unreal, not otherwise were rightly understood by the Realized One.”

english.author: kovilo
english.text: Venerable Sāriputta spoke thus.

english.author: sujato
english.text: This is what Venerable Sāriputta said.

segments.pali: Attamanā te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: With uplifted hearts, the monks were delighted with Venerable Sāriputta's speech.

english.author: sujato
english.text: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what Sāriputta said.

english.author: kovilo
english.text: The Discourse Up to Ten is complete.
